questions.stem: Who said this, ‘There shall be neither dew nor rain these years except by my word’?
questions.explanation: Elijah announced the drought to Ahab (1 Kings 17:1).

questions.stem: In the case before Solomon over the dead and the living child, the mother of the dead child supported
options: giving the living child to her opponent.
joint ownership of the living child.
King Solomon having the living child.
state ownership of the living child.
questions.explanation: She said, ‘It shall be neither mine nor yours; divide it’ (1 Kings 3:26), agreeing that the living child be cut in two.

questions.stem: Before Moses died, God appointed ... to succeed him.
questions.explanation: God told Moses to commission Joshua the son of Nun as his successor (Num. 27:18-23).

questions.stem: The treatment for those bitten by the fiery serpent was to
questions.explanation: Moses made a bronze serpent; whoever was bitten and looked at it lived (Num. 21:8-9).

questions.stem: In order that Benjamin might be brought to Egypt, Joseph detained
questions.explanation: Joseph bound Simeon before their eyes and kept him until they returned with Benjamin (Gen. 42:24).

questions.stem: When Joseph’s brothers came to him in Egypt, he said to them, ‘You are ...’
questions.explanation: Joseph accused them, ‘You are spies, you have come to see the weakness of the land’ (Gen. 42:9).

questions.stem: Sarah gave birth to ... in her old age.
questions.explanation: Sarah bore Isaac to Abraham in his old age, as God had promised (Gen. 21:1-3).

questions.stem: As a condition of his covenant with God, Abraham had to
questions.explanation: Circumcision of every male was the sign of the covenant (Gen. 17:10-11).

questions.stem: What was the condition of the earth before the creation of the world?
options: The earth was without form and void.
There was a firmament above the earth.
The heaven was very close to the earth.
The earth was inhabited by angels and spirits.
questions.explanation: ‘The earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep’ (Gen. 1:2).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: God wanted to destroy the world because
options: the sons of God were taking the daughters of men as wives.
the people made a tower of Babel to get to heaven.
the earth was filled with violence.
questions.explanation: God said to Noah, ‘the earth is filled with violence through them; behold, I will destroy them’ (Gen. 6:11-13).

questions.stem: What did Adonijah do to show that he feared Solomon? He
options: caught hold of the horns of the altar.
sent messengers to Solomon asking for a place of honour.
questions.explanation: Adonijah feared Solomon and went and caught hold of the horns of the altar (1 Kings 1:50).

questions.stem: Where did Solomon get the timber for his building?
questions.explanation: Hiram king of Tyre supplied cedars and cypress from Lebanon (1 Kings 5:6-10).

questions.stem: According to Jeremiah’s prophecy, the domination of nations by Nebuchadnezzar was
options: the result of his military might.
the result of the wickedness of nations.
the result of his righteousness and belief in God.
questions.explanation: God said he had given all these lands into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, ‘my servant’ (Jer. 27:6), so it was part of God’s purpose.

questions.stem: Ezekiel was ordered to eat ... and then go to speak to the house of Israel.
questions.explanation: ‘Eat this scroll, and go, speak to the house of Israel’ (Ezek. 3:1).

questions.topic: Obedience and Rewards: Abraham (Gen. 22:1-19), the three Hebrew youths (Dan. 3:1-30), David (1 Sam. 30:1-20)
questions.stem: The place where Abraham was asked to sacrifice Isaac was
questions.explanation: God told Abraham to go to the land of Moriah and offer Isaac there (Gen. 22:2).

questions.stem: The one who was to be the wife of Isaac was known
options: by her coming to the well to draw water.
because she was a descendant of Abraham’s brother.
because she said ‘Drink, and I will water your camels’.
questions.explanation: Abraham’s servant asked for the sign that the maiden would say, ‘Drink, and I will water your camels’ (Gen. 24:14).

questions.stem: Achan was
options: one of the spies who visited Rahab in Jericho.
one of the two men who prophesied in the camp in the wilderness.
one of the judges of Israel.
the one who took some of the devoted things when Jericho fell.
the king of the Amalekites whom Samuel hewed into pieces.
questions.explanation: Achan took some of the devoted things at Jericho and was stoned (Josh. 7:1, 25).

questions.stem: ‘How is it you were not afraid to put forth your hand to destroy the Lord’s anointed?’ was said by
options: Elijah to Ahab when Ahab sought to kill him.
David to the Amalekite who claimed to have killed Saul.
Joab to Absalom when the latter rebelled against David.
David to Saul when Saul attacked him with a spear.
questions.explanation: David said this to the Amalekite who claimed he had killed Saul (2 Sam. 1:14).

questions.stem: The prophet regularly addressed as ‘son of man’ was
questions.explanation: God repeatedly addresses Ezekiel as ‘son of man’ (e.g. Ezek. 2:1).

questions.stem: What was the last miracle God performed before the Israelites were released from Egypt?
options: Thick darkness brought about by the hot wind ‘Khamsin’.
The slaughter of all the male children.
The slaughter of the first born.
questions.explanation: The tenth plague, the death of the first-born, made Pharaoh let Israel go (Ex. 12:29-32).

questions.stem: Who was the prophet who proved on Mount Carmel that Yahweh is greater than Baal?
questions.explanation: Elijah challenged the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18).

questions.stem: On the third day of creation God made
questions.explanation: On the third day God gathered the waters and let the dry land, which he called Earth, appear, with vegetation (Gen. 1:9-13).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: The Lord said to Moses: ‘Cut two tablets of stone like the first; and I will write upon the tablets the words that were upon the first tablets which you broke.’ On what occasion was this said?
options: At the renewal of the Covenant.
Just before the election of Joshua.
After the first fall of manna from heaven.
Shortly before the conquest of Jericho.
questions.explanation: After the golden calf, God renewed the covenant and rewrote the tables (Ex. 34:1, 10).

questions.stem: The city of Jericho was captured by the Israelites
options: after a fierce battle lasting seven days.
because the army of the city was betrayed by some of its soldiers.
because the defence system was very weak.
at the blast of the trumpets of the priests.
because famine had broken out in the city and the inhabitants surrendered because of hunger.
questions.explanation: When the priests blew the trumpets and the people shouted, the wall fell down flat (Josh. 6:20).

questions.stem: The call of Isaiah took place
options: on the return from the Babylonian captivity.
in the year of the death of King Uzziah.
during the dedication of the temple by King Solomon.
shortly before the rise of the Maccabees.
after David had completely defeated the Philistines.
questions.explanation: ‘In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord’ (Isa. 6:1).

questions.stem: When Zechariah doubted the announcement of the birth of John he
questions.explanation: Gabriel told him he would be silent and unable to speak until the birth (Lk. 1:20).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: Herod wanted to kill the child Jesus because
options: he thought he would become a prophet.
he learnt that he was born king of the Jews.
he was born of a virgin.
he was born in a manger.
questions.explanation: The wise men asked for the one ‘born king of the Jews’, which troubled Herod (Mt. 2:2-3, 16).

questions.topic: Parables about love of God (Mt. 18:12-14; Lk. 15:1-32)
questions.stem: What is the main lesson of the parable of the prodigal son?
options: A son should always obey his father.
God forgives those who sincerely repent.
questions.explanation: The father’s welcome of the repentant son shows God’s forgiveness of the sinner who repents (Lk. 15:11-32).

questions.stem: ‘These men who have turned the world upside down have come here also, and Jason has received them.’ Which town is referred to here?
questions.explanation: This was the accusation against Paul and Silas at Thessalonica (Acts 17:1, 6-7).

questions.stem: ‘And you, child, will be called the prophet of the Most High’ refers to
questions.explanation: Zechariah said this of his son John in the Benedictus (Lk. 1:76).

questions.stem: The parable of the mustard seed teaches that
options: the kingdom of God is invisible.
although the kingdom of God is for all, very few enter it.
the kingdom of God will expand world-wide from what appears to be an insignificant beginning.
it is not certain when the kingdom of God will come.
the kingdom of God is within us.
questions.explanation: The smallest seed grows into a great shrub: the kingdom grows from small beginnings (Mk. 4:30-32).

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: When the women got to the tomb of Jesus they found the stone rolled away and
options: saw Jesus coming out of the tomb.
Jesus was no longer in the tomb.
Jesus was sitting in the tomb.
immediately saw a vision of Jesus.
questions.explanation: They went in and did not find the body (Lk. 24:2-3); ‘He has risen, he is not here’ (Mk. 16:6).

questions.stem: ‘You shall be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and ... and to the end of the earth.’
questions.explanation: ‘... in all Judea and Samaria and to the end of the earth’ (Acts 1:8).

questions.stem: Paul was first arrested in Jerusalem because he
questions.explanation: The Jews from Asia accused him of bringing Greeks into the temple and defiling it (Acts 21:28-30).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: Which country in Africa provided Jesus with a refuge when Herod sought to destroy him?
questions.explanation: Joseph took the child and his mother and fled to Egypt (Mt. 2:13-14).

questions.stem: ‘After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.’ Who said this?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this of Jesus (Mk. 1:7).

questions.stem: Who addressed Jesus at Jericho, saying, ‘Jesus, son of David, have mercy on me’?
questions.explanation: Blind Bartimaeus cried out to Jesus at Jericho (Mk. 10:46-47).

questions.stem: By whom did the Lord heal the blindness of Paul?
questions.explanation: Ananias laid hands on Saul and something like scales fell from his eyes (Acts 9:17-18).

questions.stem: Who insisted in his speech that God does not dwell in houses made with hands and that it was wrong for Solomon to have built a house for Him?
questions.explanation: Stephen said, ‘Solomon built a house for him. Yet the Most High does not dwell in houses made with hands’ (Acts 7:47-48).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: ‘The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the child to be born will be called holy, the Son of God.’ This was said by the angel Gabriel to
questions.explanation: Gabriel said this to Mary at the annunciation (Lk. 1:35).

questions.stem: ‘But I say to you that hear, Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you, bless those who curse you, pray for those who abuse you.’ Jesus said this
options: during the Sermon on the Mount.
questions.explanation: This is part of Jesus’ great sermon (Lk. 6:27-28; cf. Mt. 5:44), the Sermon on the Mount.

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: What did the Apostles do when complaints were made to them that some sections of the new Christian community were not being supplied with their needs for sustenance? They
options: gave out more money for buying food.
said that they had neither gold nor silver.
appointed seven deacons to undertake the care of the new Christians.
appointed the Apostles James, Peter and John to oversee the supply of provisions to the new Christians.
decided to call a council in Jerusalem to look into the matter.
questions.explanation: When the Hellenists complained about the daily distribution, seven men were chosen to serve tables (Acts 6:1-6).

questions.stem: When Paul came to Rome, the first set of people to whom he preached were the
questions.explanation: After three days Paul called together the local leaders of the Jews and spoke to them first (Acts 28:17-23).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: ‘Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.’ This was said by
questions.explanation: Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, said this to Mary (Lk. 1:42).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: Jesus was led into the wilderness by
questions.explanation: ‘Jesus was led up by the Spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil’ (Mt. 4:1).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: ‘And he came to ... where he had been brought up; and, as his custom was, he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath Day, and stood up to read.’ Identify the missing place in the above text.
questions.explanation: After the temptation Jesus came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up (Lk. 4:16).

questions.stem: ‘Therefore in the resurrection whose wife shall she be of the seven, for they all had her?’ This question was put to Jesus by the
questions.explanation: The Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection, asked this (Mt. 22:23-28).

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: Pilate gave Jesus to the Jews to be crucified because
options: he found Jesus guilty of the charges.
the Jews brought pressure upon him.
questions.explanation: Pilate found no crime in him but yielded when the crowd shouted and a riot was beginning (Mt. 27:24; Lk. 23:22-24).

questions.stem: Paul was converted so that he might
options: not be killed for his sins.
bear the name of the Lord before the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: ‘He is a chosen instrument of mine to carry my name before the Gentiles’ (Acts 9:15).

questions.stem: Paul and Silas were imprisoned at
questions.explanation: Paul and Silas were beaten and put in prison at Philippi (Acts 16:12, 23).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: After the Flood, God allowed all food to be eaten except
options: flesh with its blood in it.
questions.explanation: ‘Only you shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood’ (Gen. 9:3-4).

questions.stem: ‘Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples, born of you, shall be divided ...’ This was addressed by God to
questions.explanation: God said this to Rebekah when the twins struggled within her (Gen. 25:22-23).

questions.stem: The wife of Moses was
questions.explanation: Jethro gave Moses his daughter Zipporah (Ex. 2:21).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: ‘... I the Lord your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and the fourth generation of those who hate me, but showing steadfast love to thousands of those who love me and keep my commandments.’ This statement was made by God when
options: He gave the Ten Commandments to Moses.
the family of Aaron was elected to the priesthood.
He commanded Moses to go to meet Pharaoh.
the Israelites had settled in the Promised Land.
questions.explanation: It is part of the second commandment in the Decalogue given at Sinai (Ex. 20:5-6).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: The three sons of Noah were Shem, Ham and
questions.explanation: Noah’s sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth (Gen. 6:10).

questions.stem: For rebelling against Moses and God, the Israelites were bitten by the fiery snakes. The cure for the snakebites was
options: a drink of the water from the rock
anointing the affected part of the body with oil
to call on the name of Yahweh
a look at the bronze serpent.
questions.explanation: Whoever was bitten and looked at the bronze serpent lived (Num. 21:9).

questions.stem: Joshua was appointed to lead the Israelites to the Promised Land because
options: Moses was too old to lead them there
the Israelites preferred Joshua to Moses
Moses never returned from Mount Sinai
of Moses’ rebellion in the wilderness of Zin
questions.explanation: Because Moses rebelled against God’s word at Meribah in the wilderness of Zin, he could not enter the land, and Joshua was appointed (Num. 20:12; 27:14-18).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: The covenant was renewed on Mount Sinai because
options: there was a new generation which did not remember the first
the people had taken part in Korah’s rebellion
the people had demanded water from the rock
Aaron had made a golden calf
the people had wanted to return to Egypt.
questions.explanation: Moses broke the first tables over the golden calf, and God renewed the covenant with new tables (Ex. 32:19; 34:1, 10).

questions.stem: Those inspired by God to lead the tribes of Israel in battle were the
questions.explanation: ‘The Lord raised up judges, who saved them out of the power of those who plundered them’ (Judg. 2:16).

questions.stem: Each of the spies sent out by Moses on God’s command to report on the nature of the Promised Land was a
questions.explanation: God told Moses to send ‘from each tribe of their fathers ... every one a leader among them’ (Num. 13:2).

questions.stem: The sun stood still when
options: Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt
Jericho fell to the army of Joshua
Noah came out of the ark
Joshua defeated the Amorites at Gibeon
Moses came down from the mountain with the tables of the law.
questions.explanation: Joshua said, ‘Sun, stand thou still at Gibeon’ during the battle with the Amorite kings (Josh. 10:12-13). The paper misprints Gibeon as “Gideon”.

questions.stem: ‘I repent that I have made Saul king.’ What incident does this refer to?
options: When Saul was offering sacrifice to God
When Saul disobeyed God over Amalek
questions.explanation: God said this after Saul spared Agag and the best of the Amalekite spoil (1 Sam. 15:10-11).

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: David’s first reaction after he had been rebuked by God through the prophet Nathan for his sin against Uriah and with Uriah’s wife was to
options: plead with God to preserve the life of his child by Uriah’s wife
request that the punishments threatened by God would not come to pass
ask Nathan to beg Uriah’s wife to pardon him
simply wait for whatever God would bring on him.
questions.explanation: David at once confessed, ‘I have sinned against the Lord’ (2 Sam. 12:13; cf. Ps. 51), seeking forgiveness; pleading for the child came later.

questions.stem: ‘If he (Baal) is a god, let him contend for himself, because his altar has been pulled down.’ Who pulled down the altar?
questions.explanation: Gideon pulled down his father Joash’s altar of Baal; Joash then said these words (Judg. 6:25-32).

questions.stem: Hannah prayed to God at Shiloh for a son because
options: Elkanah hated her for being barren
she had sinned against the Lord
she wanted her son to succeed Eli.
questions.explanation: She was barren and her rival Peninnah provoked her sorely, so she wept and prayed (1 Sam. 1:6-10).

questions.stem: God pronounced utter destruction on the Amalekites because
options: they were hostile to the Kenites who lived among them
they were hostile neighbours of Israel like the Philistines
Saul desired to acquire the Amalekite territory
they opposed Israel on their way from Egypt to the promised land
God wanted to wipe out every element of Baal worship in Canaan.
questions.explanation: ‘I will punish what Amalek did to Israel in opposing them on the way, when they came up out of Egypt’ (1 Sam. 15:2).

questions.stem: As David was about to die, he charged Solomon to keep God’s statutes, commandments, ordinances and testimonies, so that he, Solomon, might
options: prosper and the Davidic dynasty be preserved for ever
have children who would succeed him
questions.explanation: ‘That you may prosper in all that you do ... that the Lord may establish his word ... there shall not fail you a man on the throne of Israel’ (1 Kings 2:3-4).

questions.stem: In the trade treaty between King Solomon and Hiram of Lebanon, Solomon was to supply wheat and oil while Hiram was to supply
questions.explanation: Hiram supplied cedar and cypress timber; Solomon gave wheat and oil (1 Kings 5:10-11).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: To whom was this addressed? ‘Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke upon us, and we will serve you.’
questions.explanation: The assembly of Israel said this to Rehoboam at Shechem (1 Kings 12:3-4).

questions.stem: ‘I have been very jealous for the Lord, the God of hosts; for the people of Israel have forsaken thy covenant, thrown down thy altars, and slain thy prophets with the sword; and I, even I only, am left; and they seek my life, to take it away.’ This was said by
options: Elijah at a cave in Mount Carmel
Moses at a cave in Mount Horeb
Elisha at a cave in Mount Nebo
Elijah at a cave in Mount Horeb
questions.explanation: Elijah fled from Jezebel to Horeb, the mount of God, and said this in a cave (1 Kings 19:8-10).

questions.stem: ‘Thus saith the Lord of Hosts, the God of Israel, Amend your ways and your doings. Trust not in lying words, saying: “The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord”.’ This message was given by
questions.explanation: This is Jeremiah’s temple sermon (Jer. 7:3-4).

questions.stem: Which prophet gave this cry? ‘Woe is me! For I am lost; for I am a man of unclean lips, and I dwell in the midst of a people of unclean lips.’
questions.explanation: Isaiah cried this at his call vision in the temple (Isa. 6:5).

questions.stem: The prophet who proclaimed a new covenant of God with Israel and Judah was
questions.explanation: ‘I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah’ (Jer. 31:31).

questions.stem: ‘And he will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of the fathers to the children.’ The person whose future work was being described here was
questions.explanation: Gabriel said this to Zechariah about his son John (Lk. 1:17).

questions.stem: He said therefore to the multitudes ... ‘You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?’ Who was the speaker?
questions.explanation: John the Baptist, son of Zechariah, said this to the crowds (Lk. 3:2, 7).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God’ was said by Jesus to
options: the leper who asked to be cleansed
the sons of Zebedee who demanded the best seats in the kingdom.
questions.explanation: Jesus answered the devil with this at the pinnacle of the temple (Mt. 4:7).

questions.stem: The people of Nazareth found it difficult to believe what Jesus preached to them because they
questions.explanation: ‘Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary?’ They took offence at him because they knew his family (Mk. 6:3).

questions.stem: In the parable of the sower, the seeds on the good ground are meant to represent those who
options: accept and live by God’s word
questions.explanation: The good soil is those who hear the word, accept it and bear fruit (Mk. 4:20).

questions.stem: Who is being referred to here? ‘But he went out and began to talk freely about it, and to spread the news, so that Jesus could no longer openly enter a town, but was out in the country; and people came to him from every quarter.’
questions.explanation: This was the leper Jesus cleansed in Galilee (Mk. 1:40-45).

questions.stem: ‘An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, but no sign shall be given to it except the sign of Jonah.’ According to St. Matthew, Jesus said this to the
questions.explanation: The Pharisees and Sadducees came to test him by asking for a sign (Mt. 16:1-4).

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: And Jesus said to them, ‘Follow me and I will make you fishers of men.’ This was addressed to
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to the brothers Simon Peter and Andrew casting their net (Mt. 4:18-19).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: Hosanna means
questions.explanation: ‘Hosanna’ is Hebrew for ‘save, we pray’ or ‘save now’.

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: Simon the Cananaean was
options: the Pharisee in whose house the woman anointed Jesus
the one who carried Jesus’ cross
one of the brothers of Jesus.
questions.explanation: Simon the Cananaean is listed among the twelve apostles (Mt. 10:4; Mk. 3:18).

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: The reason why Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went to where Jesus was buried on the third day after the burial was to
options: plead with the soldiers who were keeping watch there
see if the body of Jesus was still there
see if Jesus had risen from the dead
weep at the tomb according to the custom of the Jews.
questions.explanation: They bought spices so that they might go and anoint him (Mk. 16:1).

questions.stem: To some who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and despised others, Jesus told the parable of the
questions.explanation: The parable of the Pharisee and the tax collector was told to such people (Lk. 18:9-14).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: The main reason why Peter and John were arrested by the officers of the Temple after they had cured the lame man at the gate called Beautiful was that they
options: abused the elders of the people
disapproved of worship in the temple.
questions.explanation: The priests and Sadducees were annoyed because they were ‘proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead’ (Acts 4:1-3).

questions.stem: The conversion of Paul was made possible by
questions.explanation: The risen Jesus appeared to Saul on the Damascus road (Acts 9:3-6).

questions.stem: Who is being referred to here? ‘Let his habitation become desolate, and let there be no one to live in it’ and ‘His office let another take.’
questions.explanation: Peter applied these psalms to Judas before Matthias was chosen to replace him (Acts 1:16-20).

questions.stem: Which of the following was NOT one of the decisions of the Jerusalem Council communicated to Gentile Christians?
options: Abstinence from eating meat offered to idols.
Avoidance of eating meat with blood in it.
Abstinence from eating strangled animals’ flesh.
questions.explanation: The council did not impose circumcision; it asked Gentiles only to abstain from idol meat, blood, things strangled and unchastity (Acts 15:28-29).

questions.stem: The proconsul when Paul arrived in Corinth was called
questions.explanation: Gallio was proconsul of Achaia when the Jews brought Paul before him at Corinth (Acts 18:12).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: Identify the speaker: ‘Now, I know that the Lord has sent his angel to deliver me out of the hand of Herod and from everything that the Jewish people expected to happen to me.’
questions.explanation: Peter said this after the angel released him from prison (Acts 12:11).

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: The seven deacons were appointed to
options: conduct a mission to the Gentiles
help in the distribution of food
questions.explanation: They were appointed to serve tables in the daily distribution (Acts 6:1-3).

questions.stem: Which ruler said this in the course of Paul’s defence? ‘In a short time you think to make me a Christian!’
questions.explanation: King Agrippa said this to Paul (Acts 26:28).

questions.stem: When Paul arrived in Rome, the people he first addressed were
options: the local leaders of the Jews
the Roman soldiers who were guarding him
the pagans whom he wanted to convert
Apollos and his followers who were expecting his arrival.
questions.explanation: After three days he called together the local leaders of the Jews (Acts 28:17).

questions.stem: ‘For I am ready not only to be imprisoned but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.’ Who was this devoted person?
questions.explanation: Paul said this at Caesarea when Agabus foretold his arrest (Acts 21:13).

questions.stem: Complete the quotation which relates to Paul’s voyage to Rome: ‘Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and lo, ...’
options: Caesar will give you a favourable judgment
all who seek your life will perish
I have a large number of disciples in Rome
my name will be glorified in your mission
God has granted you all those who sail with you
questions.explanation: The angel told Paul, ‘God has granted you all those who sail with you’ (Acts 27:24).

questions.stem: According to Genesis Chapter 1, on the 6th day, God created
questions.explanation: On the sixth day God made the living creatures of the earth and created man (Gen. 1:24-31).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: The flood lasted while Noah was in the ark, for
questions.explanation: ‘The waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days’ (Gen. 7:24).

questions.stem: ‘Walk before me, and be blameless.’ How old was the addressee when this voice came?
questions.explanation: ‘When Abram was ninety-nine years old the Lord appeared to Abram, and said ... walk before me, and be blameless’ (Gen. 17:1).

questions.stem: ‘You would bring down my grey hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’ Jacob said this to his children because
options: the Ishmaelites had bought Joseph and had resold him to Potiphar
he feared that Benjamin would be lost to him like Joseph.
questions.explanation: Jacob refused to let Benjamin go to Egypt, fearing harm would befall him as it had Joseph (Gen. 42:36-38).

questions.stem: And the magicians said to Pharaoh, ‘This is the finger of God.’ This statement was made after the plague of
questions.explanation: The magicians could not produce gnats and said, ‘This is the finger of God’ (Ex. 8:16-19).

questions.stem: The father of Moses was of the tribe of
questions.explanation: ‘A man from the house of Levi went and took to wife a daughter of Levi’ (Ex. 2:1).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: When did the Israelites say ‘All that the Lord has spoken we will do’?
options: When Moses spoke to them before his death
After the incident of the golden calf
When God asked them to gather manna from heaven
questions.explanation: The people answered this at Mount Sinai when the covenant was offered and ratified (Ex. 19:8; 24:3, 7).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: The 5th of the Ten Commandments is a warning
options: not to bow down to idols
to honour one’s father and mother.
questions.explanation: The fifth commandment is ‘Honour your father and your mother’ (Ex. 20:12).

questions.stem: ‘Hear now, you rebels: shall we bring forth water for you out of this rock?’ was spoken by Moses
questions.explanation: Moses said this at Meribah in the wilderness of Zin (Num. 20:1, 10).

questions.stem: The spies sent out into the land of Canaan were NOT required to find out whether the
options: people who dwelt in it were few or many
land they dwelt in was good or bad
cities they dwelt in were camps or strongholds
land was flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Moses asked about the people (few or many), the land (good or bad), the cities (camps or strongholds) and whether there was wood in it (Num. 13:18-20), not whether it flowed with milk and honey.

questions.stem: Who was chosen to lead the Israelites after Moses’ death?
questions.explanation: Joshua succeeded Moses (Josh. 1:1-2).

questions.stem: Joshua’s first victory was in
questions.explanation: Jericho was the first city Joshua took after crossing the Jordan (Josh. 6).

questions.stem: Sisera was put to death by
questions.explanation: Jael drove a tent peg into Sisera’s temple (Judg. 4:21).

questions.stem: ‘But I will be with you and you will smite the Midianites as one man’ was said by God to
questions.explanation: The Lord said this to Gideon (Judg. 6:16).

questions.stem: The name ‘Samuel’ means
options: I have asked him of the Lord
the future prophet of the Lord.
questions.explanation: Hannah called him Samuel, ‘for she said, I have asked him of the Lord’ (1 Sam. 1:20).

questions.stem: Samuel’s sons were rejected as judges because
options: they were not from the royal family
they perverted justice and took bribes
the Israelites wanted to be like other people who had kings
questions.explanation: ‘His sons ... turned aside after gain; they took bribes and perverted justice’ (1 Sam. 8:3).

questions.stem: God took the Kingdom from Saul because he
options: did not offer sacrifices to the Lord
disobeyed the Lord by offering burnt sacrifices himself
questions.explanation: Saul offered the burnt offering himself at Gilgal instead of waiting for Samuel, and was told his kingdom would not continue (1 Sam. 13:9-14).

questions.stem: How was Saul killed?
options: He took his own sword and fell upon it.
questions.explanation: Saul, badly wounded, took his own sword and fell upon it (1 Sam. 31:4).

questions.stem: The commander of David’s army was
questions.explanation: Joab the son of Zeruiah was over David’s army (2 Sam. 8:16).

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: King David committed adultery with
questions.explanation: David lay with Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah (2 Sam. 11:2-4).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: Which prophet encouraged Jeroboam I to revolt at the initial stage?
questions.explanation: The prophet Ahijah tore his garment into twelve pieces and gave Jeroboam ten (1 Kings 11:29-31).

questions.stem: The city of Samaria was built by
questions.explanation: Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer and built the city (1 Kings 16:24).

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: The prophet from Tekoa was
questions.explanation: Amos was among the shepherds of Tekoa (Amos 1:1).

questions.stem: Which king reigned after Hezekiah?
questions.explanation: Manasseh his son reigned in Hezekiah’s stead (2 Kings 20:21).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: Jesus was said to be ‘of Nazareth’ because
options: his ancestor David lived in Nazareth
he was brought up in the city of Nazareth
he made Nazareth his preaching headquarters.
questions.explanation: Jesus grew up in Nazareth, where Joseph and Mary lived (Mt. 2:23; Lk. 2:39-40).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: Luke gave the most detailed account of Christ’s infancy because he
options: was writing an orderly account of events
copied from one of the evangelists.
questions.explanation: Luke states that he set out to write ‘an orderly account’ after following all things closely from the beginning (Lk. 1:1-4).

questions.stem: ‘You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?’ was part of the preaching of
questions.explanation: John the Baptist said this to the crowds (Lk. 3:7).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: Which of these statements is correct?
options: The order in which Jesus was tempted varies in Matthew and Luke but the tests remain the same.
Matthew follows Luke’s order in which Jesus was tempted.
The temptation story of Jesus is found in Mark only.
Only Luke gives us the story of Jesus’ temptation.
The story of Jesus’ temptation is found in Luke and John only.
questions.explanation: Matthew and Luke record the same three tests but in a different order (Mt. 4:1-11; Lk. 4:1-13).

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: Who of these was NOT one of the twelve?
questions.explanation: Luke was a companion of Paul, not one of the twelve apostles (Mt. 10:2-4).

questions.stem: Who said ‘I am not worthy to have you come under my roof’?
questions.explanation: The centurion at Capernaum said this when Jesus offered to come and heal his servant (Mt. 8:5-8).

questions.stem: ‘The kingdom of heaven is like treasure hidden in a field.’ This parable teaches about the
options: urgency of entry into the Kingdom
questions.explanation: The man sells all he has to buy the field: the kingdom is worth more than everything else (Mt. 13:44).

questions.stem: ‘This is my beloved Son; listen to him’, was said
questions.explanation: The voice from the cloud at the Transfiguration added ‘listen to him’ (Mk. 9:7).

questions.stem: ‘The kingdom of heaven may be compared to a man who sowed good seeds in his field; but while men were sleeping his enemy came and sowed weeds amongst the wheat, and went away.’ The owner of the field was
options: a son of the evil one.
questions.explanation: Jesus explained, ‘He who sows the good seed is the Son of man’ (Mt. 13:37).

questions.stem: When Herod the Tetrarch heard of the fame of Jesus, he thought that He was
options: John the Baptist raised from the dead
questions.explanation: Herod said, ‘This is John the Baptist, he has been raised from the dead’ (Mt. 14:1-2).

questions.stem: ‘Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory.’ The petitioners were
questions.explanation: James and John, the sons of Zebedee, made this request (Mk. 10:35-37).

questions.stem: ‘Today salvation has come to this house, for this is also a son of Abraham.’ This was said of
questions.explanation: Jesus said this of Zacchaeus the chief tax collector at Jericho (Lk. 19:9).

questions.stem: In the parable of the ten maidens, the five were called foolish because they
options: were sleeping before the marriage feast
did not go out to meet the bridegroom
did not take additional oil with them.
questions.explanation: The foolish took their lamps but took no oil with them (Mt. 25:3).

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: ‘I find no crime in this man.’ Who made this statement?
questions.explanation: Pilate said this to the chief priests and the multitudes (Lk. 23:4).

questions.stem: Concerning the events that will precede the end of the world, Jesus asked his followers to pray that it would not happen
questions.explanation: ‘Pray that your flight may not be in winter or on a sabbath’ (Mt. 24:20; Mk. 13:18).

questions.stem: Theophilus was
options: the one for whom the Acts of the Apostles was written
the centurion converted by Peter in Caesarea
questions.explanation: Acts opens, ‘In the first book, O Theophilus ...’ (Acts 1:1).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: And the angel said to him, ‘Dress yourself and put on your sandals.’ The addressee was
questions.explanation: The angel said this to Peter in Herod’s prison (Acts 12:7-8).

questions.stem: On the road to Gaza, Philip converted and baptized a
questions.explanation: The Ethiopian eunuch was a minister of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians (Acts 8:26-27, 38).

questions.stem: After his conversion Paul first went to
questions.explanation: Blinded, Saul was led by the hand into Damascus, where Ananias baptized him and he preached in the synagogues (Acts 9:8-20).

questions.stem: An eloquent Jew from Alexandria, well versed in the Scriptures, was
questions.explanation: ‘A Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria ... an eloquent man, well versed in the scriptures’ (Acts 18:24).

questions.stem: The ecumenical Council of A.D. 49 held in Jerusalem was mainly to discuss the
questions.explanation: The council met to decide whether Gentile converts had to be circumcised and keep the law of Moses (Acts 15:1-6).

questions.stem: An altar was set up to the Unknown God in the Greek town of
questions.explanation: Paul saw the altar ‘To an unknown god’ in Athens (Acts 17:22-23).

questions.stem: ‘You have appealed to Caesar: to Caesar then you shall go.’ This statement was made to Paul by
questions.explanation: Festus, after conferring with his council, said this (Acts 25:12).

questions.stem: The people of Malta thought that Paul must be a murderer because he
options: was bitten by a poisonous snake
was being taken to Rome as a prisoner
preached to them about the crucifixion of Jesus
was going to answer charges before Caesar.
questions.explanation: When the viper fastened on his hand, the natives said, ‘No doubt this man is a murderer’ (Acts 28:3-4).

questions.stem: ‘This at last is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; she shall be called Woman because she was ...
questions.explanation: ‘... she shall be called Woman, because she was taken out of Man’ (Gen. 2:23).

questions.stem: ‘This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven’, was said by
questions.explanation: Jacob said this after his dream of the ladder at Bethel (Gen. 28:17-19).

questions.stem: The Egyptians enslaved the Israelites and forced them to build
questions.explanation: ‘They built for Pharaoh store-cities, Pithom and Raamses’ (Ex. 1:11).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: The consecration of the people of Israel took place at the foot of Mount
questions.explanation: Moses consecrated the people, who stood at the foot of Mount Sinai (Ex. 19:14-17).

questions.stem: What occasion is reflected in this statement? ‘It is not the sound of shouting for victory, or the sound of the cry of defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear.’
options: Rejoicing for the water from the rock
Praising God after receiving the Ten Commandments
The apostasy of Aaron and the people
questions.explanation: Moses said this coming down the mountain when the people were dancing round the golden calf (Ex. 32:17-19).

questions.stem: When Moses was instructed to view the Promised Land from afar, he
options: summoned the elders and informed them about the land
prayed for a successor to shepherd the people
questions.explanation: Moses asked God to appoint a man over the congregation so that they would not be ‘as sheep which have no shepherd’ (Num. 27:12-17).

questions.stem: Who gave this advice? ‘Now therefore, fear the Lord and serve him in sincerity and faithfulness; put away the gods which your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the Lord.’
questions.explanation: Joshua said this at the covenant assembly at Shechem (Josh. 24:14).

questions.stem: To whom was this addressed? ‘Rule over us you and your son and your grandson also, for you have delivered us out of the hand of Midian.’
questions.explanation: The men of Israel said this to Gideon (Judg. 8:22).

questions.stem: Who asked this question? ‘Which is better for you that all seventy of the sons of Jerubbaal rule over you, or that one rule over you?’
questions.explanation: Abimelech, Gideon’s son, asked the men of Shechem this (Judg. 9:1-2).

questions.stem: At childhood, the word of the Lord came to Samuel because he
options: had the qualities of a prophet
was to announce the punishment for the house of Eli
questions.explanation: God called the boy Samuel to tell him the judgment he was about to bring on Eli’s house (1 Sam. 3:11-14).

questions.stem: ‘Cursed be the man who takes food before evening before I am able to avenge myself on my enemies.’ This was said by Saul during the battle between Israel and the
questions.explanation: Saul laid this oath on the people during the battle against the Philistines at Michmash (1 Sam. 14:24, 31).

questions.topic: A Man After God’s Own Heart
questions.stem: Who was the man who, in an attempt to prevent a disaster, touched the Ark and died when David was returning it to Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Uzzah put out his hand to the ark when the oxen stumbled, and God struck him (2 Sam. 6:6-7).

questions.stem: The suggestion made by the prophet Nathan to Bathsheba to foil Adonijah’s attempt to usurp the throne of David was to
options: remind David of his promise that Solomon would succeed him
have Solomon secretly anointed by Zadok
plead with Adonijah to abandon the attempt.
questions.explanation: Nathan told Bathsheba to go to David and ask, ‘Did you not swear ... Solomon your son shall reign after me?’ (1 Kings 1:11-13).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: It was wrong for King Solomon to have married foreign women because
options: they would entice him to worship idols
the women of Israel were more beautiful
a King should not have too many children
questions.explanation: God had forbidden it, ‘for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods’ (1 Kings 11:2).

questions.stem: How many months were the Israelites on forced labour in Lebanon allowed to spend at home for every month at the labour camp?
questions.explanation: ‘They would be a month in Lebanon and two months at home’ (1 Kings 5:14).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: Which of the following kings said ‘Behold your gods, O Israel, who brought you up out of the land of Egypt’?
questions.explanation: Jeroboam I said this when he set up the golden calves at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28).

questions.stem: ‘The jar of meal shall not be spent, and the cruse of oil shall not fail, until the day that the Lord sends rain upon the earth.’ From the context, which of these statements is UNTRUE?
options: The meal in the jar and the oil in the cruse were continually replenished thereafter
The widow of Zarephath prepared food for Elijah
The widow and her son ate the food and waited for their death.
The woman was gathering sticks to prepare her last meal
questions.explanation: The widow had planned to eat and die, but after Elijah’s word the meal and oil did not fail and they ate for many days (1 Kings 17:12-16).

questions.stem: Hosea said that the children of Israel shall dwell many days without king or prince, without sacrifice or pillar, without ...
questions.explanation: ‘... without sacrifice or pillar, without ephod or teraphim’ (Hos. 3:4).

questions.stem: To whom does this refer? ‘And he burned his son as an offering, and practised soothsaying and augury, and dealt with mediums and with wizards. He did much evil in the sight of the Lord, provoking him to anger.’
questions.explanation: This describes King Manasseh of Judah (2 Kings 21:6).

questions.stem: Who was the Egyptian king who not only made Eliakim king of Judah but changed Eliakim’s name to Jehoiakim?
questions.explanation: ‘Pharaoh Neco made Eliakim the son of Josiah king ... and changed his name to Jehoiakim’ (2 Kings 23:34).

questions.stem: Jeremiah wrote to the exiles in Babylon and encouraged them to
options: come back home to rebuild the temple
questions.explanation: ‘Seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile’ (Jer. 29:7).

questions.stem: Which of these prophets made this prophecy of Zion’s happy future at the return of the exiles? ‘And the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with singing; everlasting joy shall be upon their heads; they shall obtain joy and gladness, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.’
questions.explanation: This is Isaiah 35:10 (repeated in Isa. 51:11).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: ‘Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and his name shall be called Emmanuel’, which means
questions.explanation: ‘Emmanuel (which means, God with us)’ (Mt. 1:23).

questions.stem: What specific reply did John the Baptist give to the soldiers during his preaching?
options: ‘Collect no more than is appointed you’
‘Do not begin to say to yourselves, We have Abraham as our father’
questions.explanation: To the soldiers John said, ‘Rob no one by violence ... and be content with your wages’ (Lk. 3:14); option A was his reply to the tax collectors.

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: The order of the locations of Jesus’ temptations according to Matthew is
options: wilderness - high mountain - pinnacle of the temple
wilderness - pinnacle of the temple - high mountain
high mountain - wilderness - pinnacle of the temple
pinnacle of the temple - wilderness - high mountain
questions.explanation: In Matthew the tests are bread in the wilderness, then the pinnacle of the temple, then a very high mountain (Mt. 4:1-10).

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: When Christ called Levi to follow Him, he
options: waited two days before he obeyed
accounted for the tax he collected and responded
took some of the money he collected before following Him
questions.explanation: ‘And he left everything, and rose and followed him’ (Lk. 5:28).

questions.stem: The miracle which touched on ingratitude is the
questions.explanation: Of the ten lepers cleansed only one, a Samaritan, returned to give thanks (Lk. 17:11-19).

questions.stem: The parable of the unmerciful servant teaches that
options: we should exercise patience until our debtors pay us
we should forgive our debtors from our hearts
debtors should be jailed until they pay all their debts.
questions.explanation: ‘So also my heavenly Father will do to every one of you, if you do not forgive your brother from your heart’ (Mt. 18:35).

questions.stem: The ways in which various people hear the word of God are described in the parable of the
questions.explanation: The four kinds of soil in the parable of the sower stand for different hearers of the word (Mk. 4:14-20).

questions.stem: ‘But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then ...’
options: the kingdom of Satan cannot stand
the kingdom of God has come upon you
the kingdom of Satan is already divided.
questions.explanation: ‘... then the kingdom of God has come upon you’ (Mt. 12:28).

questions.stem: ‘I assure you, unless you change and become like little children, you will not enter the kingdom of God.’ This is a warning by Jesus against
questions.explanation: Jesus said this when the disciples asked who was the greatest in the kingdom, rebuking their ambition (Mt. 18:1-4).

questions.stem: Jesus taught that fasting, in addition to prayer, is necessary in some situations, during the healing of the
questions.explanation: After healing the epileptic boy Jesus said this kind comes out only by prayer and fasting (Mk. 9:29; Mt. 17:21, KJV).

questions.stem: Jesus did not grant the request of the sons of Zebedee because
options: they were not qualified for the privilege they asked for
He did not want to encourage rivalry among the disciples
it was not His to grant the request
they could not drink with Jesus’ cup.
questions.explanation: ‘To sit at my right hand and at my left is not mine to grant’ (Mt. 20:23).

questions.stem: The parable which teaches persistence in prayer is that of the
questions.explanation: Jesus told the parable of the unjust judge to show they ought always to pray and not lose heart (Lk. 18:1-8).

questions.stem: To give the widow’s mite is to give
questions.explanation: The widow ‘out of her poverty has put in everything she had’ (Mk. 12:44).

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: Which of these women was absent during the crucifixion of Jesus Christ?
questions.explanation: Mary Magdalene, Salome and Jesus’ mother are named at the cross (Mk. 15:40; Jn. 19:25); Elizabeth is not.

questions.stem: To explain the outpouring of the Holy Spirit on the day of Pentecost, Peter quoted the Prophet
questions.explanation: ‘This is what was spoken by the prophet Joel’ (Acts 2:16-21).

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: To whom was this addressed? ‘While it remained unsold, did it not remain your own? And after it was sold, was it not at your disposal? How is it that you have contrived this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men but to God.’
questions.explanation: Peter said this to Ananias (Acts 5:3-4).

questions.stem: ‘Truly I perceive that God shows no partiality’ was said by
questions.explanation: Peter said this in the house of Cornelius (Acts 10:34).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: After the killing of James the son of Zebedee, Herod also arrested Peter because
options: Peter had promised to die with Jesus
the Jews were pleased with the murder of James
Herod wanted to show his zeal for the Law of Moses
Peter was the head of the Church
questions.explanation: ‘When he saw that it pleased the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter also’ (Acts 12:3).

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: The proconsul of Paphos during the visit of Paul and Barnabas was
questions.explanation: At Paphos they met the proconsul Sergius Paulus, who believed (Acts 13:6-12).

questions.stem: Which leading men among the brethren in Jerusalem, who were themselves prophets, were sent to Antioch with a letter in the company of Paul and Barnabas?
questions.explanation: Judas called Barsabbas and Silas, leading men and prophets, carried the council’s letter (Acts 15:22, 32).

questions.stem: Lydia received Paul and Silas into her house when they came to
questions.explanation: Lydia, a seller of purple, was converted at Philippi and hosted them (Acts 16:12-15).

questions.stem: Paul, standing in the Areopagus, used the teaching of the poets of the people to introduce God the Creator at
questions.explanation: At the Areopagus in Athens Paul quoted their poets: ‘For we are indeed his offspring’ (Acts 17:22-28).

questions.stem: On his final journey to Jerusalem, Paul lodged at the house of
questions.explanation: They brought them to the house of Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple (Acts 21:16).

questions.stem: ‘In a short time you think to make me a Christian’ was said by
questions.explanation: King Agrippa said this to Paul (Acts 26:28).

questions.stem: The final port of departure for Italy where the centurion put Paul on board was
questions.explanation: At Myra in Lycia the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing for Italy and put them on board (Acts 27:5-6).

questions.stem: 'Our sister, be the mother of thousands of ten thousands; and may your descendants possess the gate of those who hate them!' Who was the sister?
questions.explanation: Rebekah's family blessed her with these words as she left to marry Isaac (Gen. 24:60).

questions.stem: 'Cast out this slave woman with her son; for the son of this slave woman shall not be heir with my son Isaac.' Who was the slave woman?
questions.explanation: Sarah asked Abraham to cast out Hagar and Ishmael (Gen. 21:10).

questions.stem: '... thorns and thistles it shall bring forth to you; and you shall eat the plants of the field. In the sweat of your face you shall eat bread.' To whom were these words spoken?
questions.explanation: God spoke these words to Adam after the fall (Gen. 3:17-19).

questions.stem: Abraham circumcised his son, Isaac, on the eighth day because
options: it was the custom of his tribe to do so
God commanded him to do so
he wanted to distinguish Isaac from Ishmael
Isaac was the son of promise
questions.explanation: Abraham circumcised Isaac when he was eight days old, 'as God had commanded him' (Gen. 21:4; cf. 17:12).

questions.stem: Who among Joseph's brothers was bound by Joseph when they went to Egypt to buy grain?
questions.explanation: Joseph took Simeon and bound him before their eyes (Gen. 42:24).

questions.stem: Joshua was buried in the hill country of
questions.explanation: Joshua was buried at Timnath-serah in the hill country of Ephraim (Josh. 24:30).

questions.stem: 'Take handfuls of ashes from the kiln, and let Moses throw them toward heaven in the sight of Pharaoh.' [This command led to]
options: the death of all Egyptian flocks and cattle
the death of the first-born of man and beast
boils and sores on man and beast
questions.explanation: The ashes thrown toward heaven became boils breaking out in sores on man and beast (Ex. 9:8-10).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: Whoever touches the 'mountain of God' shall be put to death by
questions.explanation: Whoever touched Mount Sinai was to be 'stoned or shot' (Ex. 19:12-13); shooting is the only option given.

questions.stem: 'Take off the rings of gold which are in the ears of your wives, your sons, and your daughters, and bring them to me.' [Aaron gave this instruction for]
questions.explanation: Aaron collected the gold earrings and made a molten calf (Ex. 32:2-4).

questions.stem: God commanded that Aaron should speak for Moses to the Israelites, but Moses should be to Aaron as
questions.explanation: 'He shall be a mouth for you, and you shall be to him as God' (Ex. 4:16).

questions.stem: On the first day when the Israelites left part of the bread, it bred worms and became foul, but on the sixth day when they left part of the bread it did not become foul because
options: God commanded them to keep it
Moses wanted to save them the trouble of searching for bread every day
they had discovered a better way of preserving it
questions.explanation: On the sixth day the Lord commanded them to lay up the extra for the sabbath, and it did not become foul (Ex. 16:23-24).

questions.stem: Who was regarded as the greatest prophet in the Old Testament for seeing God face to face?
questions.explanation: 'There has not arisen a prophet since in Israel like Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face' (Deut. 34:10).

questions.stem: 'Whoever rebels against your commandment and disobeys your words, whatever you command him, shall be put to death. Only be strong and of good courage.' The above passage was addressed to
questions.explanation: The people pledged this obedience to Joshua (Josh. 1:16-18).

questions.stem: Which of these statements did God make to Joshua before the crossing of the Jordan?
options: You shall lead my people with the staff of Moses in your hand
The people of Israel will murmur against you as they did to Moses
This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth
You shall select for yourself men of valour who will cross the Jordan with you
questions.explanation: God told Joshua, 'This book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth' (Josh. 1:8).

questions.stem: Achan, who took of the devoted things during the fall of Jericho, was from the tribe of
questions.explanation: Achan son of Carmi was of the tribe of Judah (Josh. 7:1, 18).

questions.stem: Who among the following people was connected with the war between Israel and King Jabin of Canaan?
questions.explanation: Jael killed Sisera, the commander of Jabin's army (Judg. 4:17-21).

questions.stem: 'Alas, my daughter! you have brought me very low, and you have become the cause of great trouble to me; for I have opened my mouth to the Lord, and I cannot take back my vow.' [The speaker was]
questions.explanation: Jephthah said this when his daughter came out to meet him after his vow (Judg. 11:35).

questions.stem: Elkanah went to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD at Shiloh
questions.explanation: Elkanah went up 'year by year' to worship and sacrifice at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:3).

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: Uriah did not wish to go down to his house because
options: Joab would set him in the forefront of the battle
the Ark was in the battle field
questions.explanation: Uriah said, 'The ark and Israel and Judah dwell in booths...; shall I then go to my house?' (2 Sam. 11:11).

questions.stem: The evil spirit that tormented Saul left him whenever he
questions.explanation: When David played the lyre, the evil spirit departed from Saul (1 Sam. 16:23).

questions.stem: Saul was made king publicly before the Lord and before all the people of Israel at
questions.explanation: 'All the people went to Gilgal, and there they made Saul king before the Lord in Gilgal' (1 Sam. 11:15).

questions.stem: When the Queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon concerning the name of the Lord, she came to test him with
questions.explanation: She came to test him with hard questions (1 Kings 10:1).

questions.stem: Besides the gift of wisdom, what other gift did the Lord promise to Solomon but with a condition?
questions.explanation: Riches and honour were promised outright; long life was promised 'if you will walk in my ways' (1 Kings 3:13-14).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: When Joseph discovered that his betrothed, Mary, was with child, he decided to divorce her quietly because
options: Mary was too tender and lovely
the angel warned Joseph not to be harsh on Mary
questions.explanation: 'Her husband Joseph, being a just man and unwilling to put her to shame, resolved to divorce her quietly' (Matt. 1:19).

questions.stem: Though Herod wanted to put John the Baptist to death, he feared the people, because they held him to be a
questions.explanation: Herod 'feared the people, because they held him to be a prophet' (Matt. 14:5).

questions.topic: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT included in the instructions given to the disciples during their mission?
questions.explanation: The twelve were told to heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse lepers and cast out demons (Matt. 10:8), not to judge the people.

questions.stem: Jesus asked his disciples not to disclose their vision of the transfiguration until the
questions.explanation: 'Tell no one the vision, until the Son of man is raised from the dead' (Matt. 17:9).

questions.stem: When Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ, Jesus replied that it had been revealed to Peter by
options: the spirit of the living God
questions.explanation: 'Flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father who is in heaven' (Matt. 16:17).

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: Which of the following prophesied the signs of the end?
questions.explanation: Jesus pointed to 'the desolating sacrilege spoken of by the prophet Daniel' as a sign of the end (Matt. 24:15; Dan. 9:27; 12:11).

questions.stem: The parable of the labourers in the vineyard teaches above all God's
questions.explanation: The householder says, 'Do you begrudge my generosity?' (Matt. 20:15); the parable shows God's generosity.

questions.stem: According to Jesus, every kingdom divided against itself is
questions.explanation: 'Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste' (Matt. 12:25).

questions.stem: Jesus taught that one should make friends quickly with one's
questions.explanation: 'Make friends quickly with your accuser, while you are going with him to court' (Matt. 5:25).

questions.stem: The Pharisees and Scribes accused the disciples of Jesus of transgressing the tradition of the elders because they
questions.explanation: 'Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat' (Matt. 15:2).

questions.stem: 'Why this waste? For this ointment might have been sold for a large sum, and given to the poor.' The event which led to this saying took place in
questions.explanation: The anointing took place in the house of Simon the leper at Bethany (Matt. 26:6-9).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: At His triumphal entry into Jerusalem, Christ had to sit on an ass because He
questions.explanation: 'This took place to fulfil what was spoken by the prophet' (Matt. 21:4-5; Zech. 9:9).

questions.stem: But Jesus answered them, 'You are wrong, because you know neither the scriptures nor the power of God. For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels in heaven.' [Jesus was answering the]
questions.explanation: This was Jesus' reply to the Sadducees, who say there is no resurrection (Matt. 22:23-30).

questions.stem: '... Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will tell the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to be burned, but gather the wheat into my barn.' This passage is on the parable of the
questions.explanation: These words come from the parable of the weeds (tares) among the wheat (Matt. 13:30).

questions.stem: 'Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall ...'
questions.explanation: '... for they shall be satisfied' (Matt. 5:6).

questions.stem: Jesus charged his disciples not to depart from Jerusalem but to wait for the promise of the Father. This promise was fulfilled when
options: the Holy Spirit filled the disciples on the day of Pentecost
the Holy Spirit descended upon Cornelius and all who heard Peter's preaching
questions.explanation: The promised Holy Spirit came upon the disciples at Pentecost (Acts 1:4-5; 2:1-4).

questions.stem: On their return to Jerusalem immediately after the Ascension, the apostles devoted themselves to
questions.explanation: 'All these with one accord devoted themselves to prayer' (Acts 1:14).

questions.stem: One of the main qualifications of the successor to Judas was that he should be a witness
options: from the time of John the Baptist
during the time of Christ's ministry and death
questions.explanation: The new apostle must 'become with us a witness to his resurrection' (Acts 1:22).

questions.stem: Peter explained that the disciples were not filled with new wine but with the Holy Spirit according to the prophecy of
questions.explanation: 'This is what was spoken by the prophet Joel' (Acts 2:16).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: Who advised the Sanhedrin to keep away from the apostles and let them alone?
questions.explanation: Gamaliel said, 'Keep away from these men and let them alone' (Acts 5:34-38).

questions.stem: Saul travelled to Damascus in order to
options: obtain letters of authority from the High Priest
arrest those belonging to the Way
questions.explanation: He went so that 'if he found any belonging to the Way... he might bring them bound to Jerusalem' (Acts 9:2).

questions.stem: Peter was criticized by the circumcision party in Jerusalem because he
questions.explanation: 'Why did you go to uncircumcised men and eat with them?' (Acts 11:2-3).

questions.stem: Who prophesied a great famine over all the world at Antioch?
questions.explanation: Agabus foretold a great famine over all the world (Acts 11:27-28).

questions.stem: 'While Peter was still saying this, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard the word.' Where did this happen?
questions.explanation: It happened in the house of Cornelius at Caesarea (Acts 10:24, 44).

questions.stem: 'Then they cast him out of the city and stoned him; and the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.' [The man stoned was]
questions.explanation: This describes the stoning of Stephen (Acts 7:58).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: The reference in Genesis chapter 6 to the union between the 'sons of God' and the 'daughters of men' explains the origin of
questions.explanation: Their children 'were the mighty men that were of old, the men of renown' (Gen. 6:4).

questions.stem: 'Two nations' in Rebekah's womb refers to the
questions.explanation: Esau (Edom) and Jacob (Israel) were the two nations in her womb (Gen. 25:23-26).

questions.stem: Joseph's rough treatment of his brothers was to
options: assure himself that they were not spies
questions.explanation: Joseph tested his brothers until they showed repentance for what they had done to him (Gen. 42:21; 44:16-34).

questions.stem: Which of the following BEST describes Abraham's reaction to God's promise of a son by Sarah?
questions.explanation: Abraham fell on his face and laughed, doubting that a son could be born to a man of a hundred and to Sarah at ninety (Gen. 17:17).

questions.stem: Mahanaim is so called because Jacob saw the angels of God as God's
questions.explanation: Jacob said, 'This is God's army!' and called the place Mahanaim (Gen. 32:1-2).

questions.stem: 'I have sinned this time; the Lord is in the right, and I and my people are in the wrong.' Pharaoh said this after the plague of
questions.explanation: Pharaoh said this during the plague of hail (Ex. 9:23-27).

questions.stem: The request of Moses that Israel should be allowed to go and worship God was interpreted by Pharaoh to mean
questions.explanation: Pharaoh said, 'You are idle, you are idle; therefore you say, Let us go and sacrifice' (Ex. 5:8, 17).

questions.stem: The Passover lamb was to be kept until the fourteenth day of the first month when the whole assembly was to kill their lambs
questions.explanation: They were to kill their lambs 'in the evening' (Ex. 12:6).

questions.stem: Pharaoh's horsemen and his army overtook the fleeing Hebrews, encamped by the sea, at
questions.explanation: They overtook them encamped at the sea, by Pi-hahiroth (Ex. 14:9).

questions.stem: The sin of the Israelites that led to the punishment by fiery serpents was
options: trying to stone Caleb and Joshua
questions.explanation: 'The people spoke against God and against Moses', and the Lord sent fiery serpents (Num. 21:5-6).

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: During the confirmation of the covenant, Moses was invited by the Lord along with
questions.explanation: 'Come up to the Lord, you and Aaron, Nadab, and Abihu, and seventy of the elders' (Ex. 24:1).

questions.stem: 'Go into the hills, lest the pursuers meet you; and hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers have returned; then afterward you may go your way.' Who gave this advice?
questions.explanation: Rahab gave this advice to the two spies (Josh. 2:16).

questions.stem: When Joshua burned Ai, he also put to death the king of Ai by
questions.explanation: 'He hanged the king of Ai on a tree until evening' (Josh. 8:29).

questions.stem: In Jotham's parable of the trees, Abimelech is likened to the
questions.explanation: The bramble, which accepted kingship, represents Abimelech (Judg. 9:14-15).

questions.stem: The preservation of the twelve stones by Joshua in Gilgal was to
options: remind Israel of the crossing of the River Jordan
indicate that the site was a quarry
questions.explanation: The stones were a memorial that Israel crossed the Jordan on dry ground (Josh. 4:20-23).

questions.stem: Samson, as a Nazirite, was required to avoid alcohol,
questions.explanation: He was to drink no wine, eat nothing unclean, and no razor was to come upon his head (Judg. 13:4-5).

questions.stem: Which city was captured by Joshua before the disaster at Ai?
questions.explanation: Jericho fell (Josh. 6) before the defeat at Ai (Josh. 7).

questions.stem: 'I have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and I have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.' This declaration was made by
questions.explanation: Saul said this to Samuel (1 Sam. 15:20).

questions.stem: 'O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt ... give to thy maidservant a son, then I will give him to the Lord all the days of his life, and no razor shall touch his head.' Who said this?
questions.explanation: This was Hannah's vow at Shiloh (1 Sam. 1:11).

questions.stem: Eli fell down and died because of the
options: capture of the Ark of the Covenant
questions.explanation: When the messenger mentioned the ark of God, Eli fell backward and died (1 Sam. 4:18).

questions.stem: 'Then Saul fell at once full length upon the ground, filled with fear because of the words of Samuel; and there was no strength in him ...' This happened when Samuel
options: told Saul that God had rejected him and had chosen David to be king
condemned Saul for offering sacrifice before his arrival
questions.explanation: This happened at Endor after the medium brought up Samuel (1 Sam. 28:20).

questions.topic: A Man After God’s Own Heart
questions.stem: Amnon's incest with Tamar marks the beginning of
options: the intrigues for succession to the throne
questions.explanation: Amnon's crime led to Absalom killing Amnon and later rebelling, the start of the struggle for David's throne (2 Sam. 13-15).

questions.topic: A Man After God’s Own Heart
questions.stem: As David took to flight from Jerusalem on account of Absalom's conspiracy, he was apprehensive of the role of
questions.explanation: David prayed, 'O Lord, I pray thee, turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness' (2 Sam. 15:31).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: To whom did God promise to give the kingdom after Solomon's heart turned away from the Lord?
questions.explanation: Through Ahijah, God promised ten tribes to Jeroboam (1 Kings 11:29-31).

questions.stem: What did Solomon provide for Hiram in exchange for timber of cedar and cypress?
questions.explanation: Solomon gave Hiram wheat and oil as food for his household (1 Kings 5:10-11).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: The gift of gold to the infant Jesus indicated his
questions.explanation: Gold, a gift fit for a king, points to Jesus' kingship (Matt. 2:2, 11).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: Herod ordered the killing of children when he
options: learnt that a king was born
had been tricked by the wise men
could not see the new baby
searched in vain for the wise men
questions.explanation: 'When Herod saw that he had been tricked by the wise men, he was in a furious rage' and killed the children (Matt. 2:16).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: 'And you, O Bethlehem, in the land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you shall come a ruler who will govern my people Israel.' This statement fulfils the prophecy of
questions.explanation: Matt. 2:6 quotes Micah 5:2.

questions.topic: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)
questions.stem: According to Mark, what were the disciples forbidden to take for their journey?
questions.explanation: 'Take nothing for their journey except a staff; no bread, no bag, no money in their belts' (Mark 6:8).

questions.stem: How many days elapsed between Peter's confession and the transfiguration?
questions.explanation: 'After six days Jesus took with him Peter and James and John' (Matt. 17:1; Mark 9:2).

questions.stem: The young man who wanted to know from Jesus what good deed would qualify him for heaven 'went away sorrowful' because he
options: was uncertain about treasure in heaven
would realize little money from the sale of his goods
questions.explanation: 'He went away sorrowful; for he had great possessions' (Matt. 19:22).

questions.stem: In St. Matthew's record of the ethical teaching of Jesus (chapters 5-7), the most important divine demand that will enable a man to inherit the kingdom of God is
questions.explanation: 'Not every one who says to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter the kingdom of heaven, but he who does the will of my Father' (Matt. 7:21).

questions.stem: The answer 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God' was made by Peter in the neighbourhood of
questions.explanation: Peter's confession took place in the district of Caesarea Philippi (Matt. 16:13-16).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: 'You shall not tempt the Lord your God.' To which temptation did Jesus give this reply?
questions.explanation: Jesus replied this when the devil told him to throw himself down from the pinnacle of the temple (Matt. 4:5-7).

questions.stem: Which of these parables teaches about judgement and separation?
questions.explanation: In the parable of the net the good fish are separated from the bad, as the angels will separate the evil from the righteous (Matt. 13:47-50).

questions.stem: 'If any one would be first, he must be last of all and servant of all.' What does this saying of Jesus teach?
questions.explanation: Jesus taught humble service as true greatness (Mark 9:35).

questions.stem: The appearance of Elijah and Moses at the transfiguration indicates the significance of the
questions.explanation: Moses represents the Law and Elijah the Prophets, both bearing witness to Jesus.

questions.stem: One of the illustrations of Jesus on true greatness is
questions.explanation: 'Whoever humbles himself like this child, he is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven' (Matt. 18:4).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: From which town did Jesus send two of his disciples to make adequate preparation for the last entry into Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: 'When they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage... Jesus sent two disciples' (Matt. 21:1).

questions.stem: Which religious groups asked Jesus about payment of taxes to Caesar?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees sent their disciples with the Herodians to ask him (Matt. 22:15-17; Mark 12:13).

questions.stem: When the Pharisees accused Jesus' disciples of plucking heads of grain on the Sabbath, Jesus referred them to what David did during the high priesthood of
questions.explanation: '... when Abiathar was high priest' (Mark 2:26).

questions.stem: 'Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.' This leaven is their
questions.explanation: 'He did not tell them to beware of the leaven of bread, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees' (Matt. 16:12).

questions.stem: The three thousand converts on the day of Pentecost devoted themselves to
options: the breaking of bread and the prayers
questions.explanation: 'They devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching and fellowship, to the breaking of bread and the prayers' (Acts 2:42).
