questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: Two of the seven deacons are
questions.explanation: The seven were Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas and Nicolaus (Acts 6:5).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: According to the apostles' speech before the Sanhedrin, the Holy Spirit is given by God to
questions.explanation: '... the Holy Spirit whom God has given to those who obey him' (Acts 5:32).

questions.stem: In his speech concerning the replacement of Judas Iscariot, Peter quoted from
questions.explanation: 'For it is written in the book of Psalms...' (Acts 1:20).

questions.stem: One of the seven Hellenists who preached the gospel in Samaria, and from Azotus to Caesarea, was
questions.explanation: Philip preached in Samaria and from Azotus to Caesarea (Acts 8:5, 40).

questions.stem: Simon the magician was rebuked by Peter in Samaria because he
options: perverted the minds of the people
opposed the teaching of the apostles
wanted to purchase spiritual power with money
questions.explanation: Simon offered money for the power to give the Holy Spirit (Acts 8:18-20).

questions.stem: The disciples were for the first time called Christians in
questions.explanation: 'In Antioch the disciples were for the first time called Christians' (Acts 11:26).

questions.stem: 'Then the Lord God said, "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a ... fit for him."' [Fill the gap]
questions.explanation: 'I will make him a helper fit for him' (Gen. 2:18).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: The first generation of mankind was destroyed in the great flood of water because of
questions.explanation: 'The earth was corrupt in God's sight, and the earth was filled with violence' (Gen. 6:11-13).

questions.stem: Which of the following is the sign of the covenant between God and Abraham?
options: The sprinkling of blood on door posts
Circumcision in the flesh of the foreskins
questions.explanation: Circumcision was 'a sign of the covenant between me and you' (Gen. 17:11).

questions.stem: God appeared to Jacob in a dream and Jacob made a vow to
questions.explanation: At Bethel Jacob vowed, 'of all that thou givest me I will give the tenth to thee' (Gen. 28:22).

questions.stem: Joseph saw his sale by his brothers as God's plan to enable him to
questions.explanation: 'God sent me before you to preserve life' (Gen. 45:5).

questions.stem: The two Hebrew midwives instructed by Pharaoh to kill the Hebrew male babies at birth were
questions.explanation: The midwives were Shiphrah and Puah (Ex. 1:15).

questions.stem: The Egyptian magicians were able to reproduce the first three miracles done by Moses and Aaron, but the fourth which they were unable to perform was the plague of
questions.explanation: The magicians copied the rod-serpent, the blood and the frogs, but could not bring forth gnats (Ex. 8:18).

questions.stem: The possibility of crossing the Red Sea was seen by Israel as
options: God's active presence in their midst
the miraculous power of Moses' rod
questions.explanation: 'Israel saw the great work which the Lord did... and the people feared the Lord; and they believed in the Lord' (Ex. 14:31).

questions.stem: In Exodus 17 and Numbers 20, similar incidents of lack of water for the congregation are recorded. A significant difference, however, is that in Exodus 17, Moses is commanded to
questions.explanation: In Ex. 17:6 Moses is told to strike the rock; in Num. 20:8 he is told to speak to it.

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: The only commandment which has a promise attached to it concerns
options: not taking the name of the Lord in vain
questions.explanation: 'Honour your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land' (Ex. 20:12; Eph. 6:2).

questions.stem: 'Draw your sword and kill me, lest men say of me, "A woman killed him."' The speaker was
questions.explanation: Abimelech said this to his armour-bearer after a woman threw a millstone on him (Judg. 9:53-54).

questions.stem: A famous prophetess who was also a judge in Israel was
questions.explanation: 'Deborah, a prophetess... was judging Israel at that time' (Judg. 4:4).

questions.stem: Gideon was also called Jerubbaal because he
options: pulled down the altar of Baal and cut down the Asherah beside it
led the Israelites against the Midianites who were Baal worshippers
turned Israel away from Baal worship
questions.explanation: He was called Jerubbaal, 'Let Baal contend against him, because he pulled down his altar' (Judg. 6:28-32).

questions.stem: Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom because
options: he did everything as the Lord had commanded him
Moses had laid his hands upon him
the Lord had promised to be with him as He was with Moses
he meditated on the book of the law day and night
questions.explanation: 'Joshua was full of the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him' (Deut. 34:9).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: 'My little finger is thicker than my father's loins' means that in comparison with his father, Rehoboam would
questions.explanation: Rehoboam meant he would be harsher than Solomon (1 Kings 12:10-11).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: 'What portion have we in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. To your tents, O Israel!' This declaration marked the end of the
questions.explanation: With this cry the northern tribes broke away from Rehoboam, ending the united kingdom (1 Kings 12:16).

questions.stem: The incident which inspired King Josiah to undertake a reform was the
options: discovery of the book of the law
questions.explanation: Hilkiah found the book of the law in the temple, and its reading moved Josiah to reform (2 Kings 22:8-13).

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: 'Seek good, and not evil, that you may live; and so the Lord, the God of hosts, will be with you, as you have said.' Which prophet gave this advice?
questions.explanation: Amos 5:14.

questions.stem: 'And at the time of the offering of the oblation, Elijah the prophet came near and said, "... Answer me, O Lord, answer me, that this people may know that thou, O Lord, art God, and that thou hast turned their hearts back."' What happened after this prayer?
options: The fire of the Lord fell
questions.explanation: 'Then the fire of the Lord fell, and consumed the burnt offering' (1 Kings 18:36-38).

questions.stem: One of the reasons why Sennacherib could not enter Jerusalem and conquer it as he did to Samaria was that
options: his god told him to return home from his camp
thousands of his soldiers miraculously died overnight
he willingly changed his mind and returned to his country
fighting broke out among his soldiers
questions.explanation: The angel of the Lord slew 185,000 Assyrians in one night (2 Kings 19:35-36).

questions.stem: When the Chaldean army captured King Zedekiah, they
options: slew his wives before his eyes
cut off his fingers and toes
questions.explanation: They slew his sons before his eyes, put out his eyes and bound him in fetters (2 Kings 25:7).

questions.stem: 'All we like sheep have gone astray; we have turned every one to his own way; and the Lord has laid on him the iniquity of us all.' This messianic prophecy was made by
questions.explanation: Isaiah 53:6.

questions.stem: The vision of 'dry bones' teaches that
options: there will be a resurrection of the body
there will be a new creation
questions.explanation: 'These bones are the whole house of Israel... I will bring you home into the land of Israel' (Ezek. 37:11-14).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: The Gilgamesh Epic is the Babylonian equivalent of the biblical story of the
questions.explanation: The Gilgamesh Epic contains a Babylonian flood story parallel to Genesis 6-9.

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: To whom was the birth of Jesus announced with a sign?
questions.explanation: The angel told the shepherds, 'This will be a sign for you: you will find a babe wrapped in swaddling cloths' (Luke 2:12).

questions.stem: The central message of John the Baptist in the Jordan region was about a baptism
questions.explanation: John preached 'a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins' (Luke 3:3).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: Jesus heard a voice saying: 'Thou art my beloved Son; with thee I am well pleased.' Jesus heard this voice during His
questions.explanation: These words were spoken at his baptism (Mark 1:11; Luke 3:22).

questions.stem: According to Herod, Jesus was John the Baptist raised from the dead because He
options: was a prophet like one of the prophets
had the powers of John at work in Him
questions.explanation: Herod said, 'John the baptizer has been raised from the dead; that is why these powers are at work in him' (Mark 6:14).

questions.stem: When John sent his disciples to ask Jesus, 'Are you he who is to come...?', Jesus' immediate reaction was to
options: ask them to tell John about his miracles
speak to the crowds concerning John
ask the crowds what they went into the wilderness to see
questions.explanation: 'In that hour he cured many of diseases...; and he answered them, Go and tell John what you have seen' (Luke 7:21-22).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: 'Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among men with whom he is pleased!' is usually referred to as
questions.explanation: This is the song of the heavenly host to the shepherds (Luke 2:13-14).

questions.stem: 'I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.' This statement was made during the healing of the
questions.explanation: Jesus said this of the centurion whose servant he healed (Luke 7:9).

questions.stem: When they saw the man who had been possessed by demons in his right mind, the Gerasenes
options: asked Jesus to depart from them
asked Jesus to stay on with them
questions.explanation: 'They began to beg Jesus to depart from their neighbourhood' (Mark 5:15-17).

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: One of the objectives, according to Mark, for which Jesus appointed the twelve was for them to
options: make disciples of all the nations of the earth
denounce the hypocrisy of the Pharisees and the Sadducees
questions.explanation: He appointed twelve to be with him, to be sent out to preach 'and have authority to cast out demons' (Mark 3:14-15).

questions.stem: 'Get behind me, Satan! For you are not on the side of God, but of men.' The reason for this sharp rebuke was that the addressee
options: confessed that Jesus is the Christ
wanted to dissuade Jesus from dying on the cross
desired to be at the right hand of Christ
questions.explanation: Peter rebuked Jesus for predicting his suffering and death (Mark 8:31-33).

questions.stem: From the parable of the friend at midnight we learn that
options: we should always make our requests even at midnight
we cannot receive anything from God if we don't ask
an evil father will always give good gifts to his children
the heavenly Father will always give the Holy Spirit to anybody
questions.explanation: The parable ends, 'Ask, and it will be given you... for every one who asks receives' (Luke 11:5-10); the Spirit is given 'to those who ask him' (v.13).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: 'And he was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered to him.' Jesus was led into the wilderness by
questions.explanation: 'The Spirit immediately drove him out into the wilderness' (Mark 1:12).

questions.stem: Which of the following instructions was given only to the seventy and not to the twelve when Jesus sent His disciples on missions?
options: Wipe off the dust from their feet
Salute no one on the road
questions.explanation: Only the seventy were told to 'salute no one on the road' (Luke 10:4); shaking off dust and taking no bag were told to both.

questions.stem: 'But new wine must be put into fresh wineskins.' What issue was raised to which this statement was a response?
questions.explanation: Jesus said this in answer to the question why his disciples did not fast (Luke 5:33-38).

questions.stem: 'Then render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.' The above quotation teaches
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that civil duties such as taxes should be paid (Luke 20:25).

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: Who requested the body of Jesus after His death?
questions.explanation: Joseph of Arimathea asked Pilate for the body (Luke 23:50-52).

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: 'Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked to us ...?' This expresses the regret of
questions.explanation: The two disciples on the road to Emmaus said this (Luke 24:18, 32).

questions.stem: Paul was accused of apparently being a preacher of foreign divinities in Athens because he preached Jesus and the
questions.explanation: 'He seems to be a preacher of foreign divinities - because he preached Jesus and the resurrection' (Acts 17:18).

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: When Paul and Barnabas healed a cripple at Lystra, the people named them
questions.explanation: 'Barnabas they called Zeus, and Paul... Hermes' (Acts 14:12, RSV).

questions.stem: Paul told the Athenians that they were very religious because
options: some of their poets said that men are the offspring of God
they dedicated an altar to the Unknown God
their Epicurean and Stoic philosophers always discussed religious issues
the city was full of idols and symbols of religious devotion
questions.explanation: 'I perceive that in every way you are very religious. For... I found also an altar with this inscription, To an unknown god' (Acts 17:22-23).

questions.stem: The elders at Jerusalem advised Paul on his arrival in the city to
options: purify himself along with men under vows
join those in the temple for prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: They told him to purify himself with four men under a vow (Acts 21:23-24).

questions.stem: 'Do not be afraid, but speak and do not be silent; for I am with you, and no man shall attack you to harm you; for I have many people in this city.' [In which city was Paul given this assurance?]
questions.explanation: The Lord spoke to Paul in a vision at Corinth (Acts 18:1, 9-10).

questions.stem: To the question of the Philippian jailer, 'Men, what must I do to be saved?', Paul replied,
options: confess your sins and give alms
release us and wash our wounds
trust in God and pray always
questions.explanation: 'Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved' (Acts 16:31).

questions.stem: 'Let it be known to you then that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles; they will listen.' This implies that
options: the Gentiles will be more receptive to Christianity than the Jews
the Jews have lost the opportunity of salvation forever
Paul has completely lost hope in the Jews
questions.explanation: Paul said this in Rome when many Jews disbelieved, meaning the Gentiles would receive the gospel more readily (Acts 28:24-28).

questions.stem: During the voyage to Rome, some people thought that Paul was a god because
options: he was not harmed by a viper
questions.explanation: When the viper did him no harm, the people of Malta said he was a god (Acts 28:3-6).

questions.stem: 'Be fruitful and multiply ...' This statement occurs first in Genesis following the creation of
questions.explanation: God first blessed the sea creatures and birds with 'Be fruitful and multiply' (Gen. 1:20-22), before saying it to man (v.28).

questions.stem: The four promises of God to Abram were land,
options: many descendants, greatness and medium of blessings
questions.explanation: God promised land, a great nation (descendants), a great name, and that through him all families would be blessed (Gen. 12:1-3, 7).

questions.stem: 'God has made laughter for me; every one who hears will laugh over me.' This statement was made at the birth of
questions.explanation: Sarah said this at the birth of Isaac (Gen. 21:6).

questions.stem: When the Israelites were caught between Pharaoh's army and the Red Sea, God instructed Moses to
options: command the sea to be divided
throw his rod into the sea
stretch out his hand over the sea
questions.explanation: 'Lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it' (Ex. 14:16, 21).

questions.stem: 'Who is the Lord, that I should heed his voice and let Israel go? I do not know the Lord, and moreover I will not let Israel go.' [What did Pharaoh do to the Israelites after saying this?]
options: He appealed to them to stay in Egypt
questions.explanation: Pharaoh made them gather their own straw while keeping the same tally of bricks (Ex. 5:2-9).

questions.stem: Which of the following is a condition for the eating of the Passover?
options: A fatted lamb should be taken from among the sheep or goats
Anything that remained until morning should be burnt
The lamb should be eaten boiled with its head, legs and inner parts
It should not be eaten in haste
questions.explanation: 'You shall let none of it remain until the morning, anything that remains until the morning you shall burn' (Ex. 12:10); it was to be roasted and eaten in haste.

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: Before God met with Israel at Mount Sinai, Moses charged his people not to
options: tremble at the sight of smoke
tremble at the sound of thunder
questions.explanation: Moses said to the people, 'Be ready by the third day; do not go near a woman' (Ex. 19:15).

questions.stem: 'It is not the sound of shouting for victory, or the sound of the cry of defeat, but the sound of singing that I hear.' [This was said at the time of the]
options: consecration of the Israelites at Mount Sinai
questions.explanation: Moses said this as he came down and heard the people worshipping the golden calf (Ex. 32:18-19).

questions.stem: In order to stay alive, anyone who was bitten by the fiery serpent had to
questions.explanation: 'If a serpent bit any man, he would look at the bronze serpent and live' (Num. 21:9).

questions.stem: '... As I was with Moses, so I will be with you; I will not fail you or forsake you ...' In the above passage, God addresses
questions.explanation: God spoke these words to Joshua (Josh. 1:5).

questions.stem: The cities of the Amorites were completely devastated by Israel through the combined forces of
questions.explanation: The Lord threw them into a panic, Israel slew them with the sword, and the Lord threw down great hailstones (Josh. 10:10-11).

questions.stem: In which of the Philistine cities did Samson carry away on his shoulders the doors, posts and bar of the city gate?
questions.explanation: Samson took the doors of the gate of Gaza (Judg. 16:1-3).

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: The king that reigned in Samaria during the prophecies of Amos and Hosea was
questions.explanation: Both prophesied 'in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel' (Amos 1:1; Hos. 1:1).

questions.stem: The king who disguised himself when he went to Ramoth-gilead was
questions.explanation: Ahab disguised himself and went into battle at Ramoth-gilead (1 Kings 22:29-30).

questions.stem: Which of the following kings built the city of Samaria?
questions.explanation: Omri bought the hill of Samaria from Shemer and built the city (1 Kings 16:24).

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: The theme of Amos's prophecies centres on the
questions.explanation: Amos stressed God's righteousness and demanded justice: 'let justice roll down like waters, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream' (Amos 5:24).

questions.stem: The event which ultimately led to the destruction of the Northern Kingdom was the invasion of
questions.explanation: When Syria and Israel attacked Jerusalem, Ahaz called in Assyria (2 Kings 16:5-9), which then crushed Damascus and later destroyed Samaria (2 Kings 17).

questions.stem: What was King Hezekiah's reaction to the letter of threat from the Assyrian king?
options: He spread it before God in the temple and prayed
He sent for his fellow kings to come and assist him
He summoned his soldiers to fight the Assyrians
He sent to the prophets for advice
questions.explanation: Hezekiah spread the letter before the Lord in the temple and prayed (2 Kings 19:14-15).

questions.stem: Manasseh did what was evil in the sight of the Lord because he
options: waged wars against the people of God
questions.explanation: Manasseh rebuilt the high places, erected altars for Baal and set up idols (2 Kings 21:2-7).

questions.stem: Who was the last king of Judah that suffered at the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah, the last king of Judah, was blinded and taken to Babylon (2 Kings 25:7).

questions.stem: The image of jealousy which Ezekiel saw was the
options: worship of Baal in the land of Israel
questions.explanation: The image of jealousy at the temple gate was one of the abominations committed in the house of the Lord (Ezek. 8:3-6).

questions.topic: Response to the state of Judah (Neh. 2; 4:1-23; Ezra 3:4; 5; 6; 7)
questions.stem: What reason did the people around Jerusalem give for wanting to assist the returned exiles in rebuilding the temple?
options: They shared the same geographical location with the Jews
They themselves were Jews by descent
They were commanded to do so by King Cyrus of Persia
They also worshipped the same God as the Jews
questions.explanation: 'Let us build with you; for we worship your God as you do' (Ezra 4:2).

questions.stem: Jeremiah's vision of the rod of almond was meant to symbolize that God
options: would protect Jeremiah at all times
would confirm His word through Jeremiah
would send evil from the North upon the people
had appointed Jeremiah as a prophet before his birth
questions.explanation: 'I am watching over my word to perform it' (Jer. 1:11-12).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: '... Did you not know that I must be in my Father's house?' [Jesus said this to]
questions.explanation: The boy Jesus said this to his parents when they found him in the temple (Luke 2:48-49).

questions.stem: '... Rob no one by violence or by false accusation, and be content with your wages.' [John the Baptist gave this instruction to the]
questions.explanation: John said this to the soldiers (Luke 3:14).

questions.stem: James and John caused the other disciples of Jesus to be angry because they
options: did not go with the others on the missionary journey
asked for a special favour to sit with Jesus in glory
defected to join the disciples of John the Baptist
questions.explanation: When the ten heard their request to sit at his right and left in glory, they were indignant (Mark 10:37-41).

questions.topic: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)
questions.stem: What is the significance of Jesus allowing His disciples to take certain things and not others on their missionary journey to the evangelist?
options: Adequate material and spiritual preparation should be made for the work
He should depend on his audience for every need
He should have absolute confidence in the sufficiency of God
He should not leave a place where he is not received without placing a curse on the people
questions.explanation: By taking almost nothing, the disciples were to rely wholly on God's provision (Mark 6:8-9; Luke 9:3).

questions.stem: '... Moses and Elijah, who appeared in glory and spoke of his departure ...' [The 'departure' referred to the]
questions.explanation: They 'spoke of his departure, which he was to accomplish at Jerusalem', i.e. his death (Luke 9:31).

questions.stem: Jesus pronounced 'woe' on the rich during the sermon on the plain because they
options: had received their reward on earth
questions.explanation: 'Woe to you that are rich, for you have received your consolation' (Luke 6:24).

questions.stem: In the parable of the sower, the seeds that fell on the rock represent people who
options: believed for a short while and later fell away
believed and were later enticed by riches
questions.explanation: 'They believe for a while and in time of temptation fall away' (Luke 8:13).

questions.stem: 'Good Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?' [Jesus' answer required the man to]
options: keep the commandments and surrender his wealth
keep the commandments and pay tithe
do to others as he wished others to do to him
questions.explanation: Jesus pointed him to the commandments and told him to sell all he had and give to the poor (Mark 10:17-21).

questions.stem: 'Go your way; your faith has made you well.' This statement was addressed to
options: the woman with the issue of blood
questions.explanation: Jesus said to blind Bartimaeus, 'Go your way; your faith has made you well' (Mark 10:52); to the woman he said, 'Daughter... go in peace'.

questions.stem: The disciples could not cast out the dumb spirit because
options: they were not familiar with that particular spirit
it could only be driven out by prayer
questions.explanation: 'This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer' (Mark 9:29).

questions.stem: Which of the following did NOT believe in the resurrection of the dead?
questions.explanation: 'The Sadducees... say that there is no resurrection' (Mark 12:18; Acts 23:8).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: The Holy Week starts with the
questions.explanation: Holy Week begins on Palm Sunday with the triumphal entry into Jerusalem.

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: Where did Jesus go after His triumphal entry into Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: After looking round the temple, 'he went out to Bethany with the twelve' (Mark 11:11).

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: Pilate delivered Jesus to be crucified because he
options: was afraid of the chief priests
questions.explanation: 'Pilate, wishing to satisfy the crowd... delivered him to be crucified' (Mark 15:15).

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: The two disciples on the way to Emmaus recognized Jesus
options: before they got to the village
at the breaking of bread while at table
questions.explanation: 'He was known to them in the breaking of the bread' (Luke 24:30-35).

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: 'Then after fasting and praying they laid their hands on them and sent them off.' The significance of the laying on of hands in this passage is that
options: the Church under the guidance of the Holy Spirit initiated the missionary work of Paul and Barnabas
the teachers' and prophets' hands conferred authority on Paul and Barnabas
the apostles Paul and Barnabas were here ordained priests
Paul and Barnabas were here confirmed Christians and the first apostles
questions.explanation: At the Spirit's command the church at Antioch set apart and sent out Barnabas and Saul (Acts 13:2-4).

questions.stem: The reason for the first Apostolic Council in Jerusalem was that
options: circumcision was enjoined on the Gentile converts as necessary for salvation
the Gentiles were discriminated against at the fellowship meals
the widows of Hellenistic Jews were discriminated against in the daily distribution
questions.explanation: Men from Judea taught, 'Unless you are circumcised... you cannot be saved' (Acts 15:1-2).

questions.stem: Before the Areopagus, Paul declared that the Unknown God was
options: a manifestation of the human mind
questions.explanation: 'The God who made the world and everything in it' (Acts 17:23-24).

questions.stem: Owing to the uproar in Jerusalem, the tribune ordered Paul to be examined by scourging, but changed his mind when he discovered that Paul was
questions.explanation: The tribune was afraid when he learned Paul was a Roman citizen (Acts 22:24-29).

questions.stem: When Paul and his companions were shipwrecked, the soldiers planned to kill the prisoners, but the centurion prevented them because
options: they would have to account for them
he wanted to save Paul's life
it was not lawful to kill
questions.explanation: 'The centurion, wishing to save Paul, kept them from carrying out their purpose' (Acts 27:42-43).

questions.stem: '... You shall indeed hear but never understand, and you shall indeed see but never perceive.' To which prophet did Paul attribute this saying?
questions.explanation: 'The Holy Spirit was right in saying to your fathers through Isaiah the prophet' (Acts 28:25-26; Isa. 6:9).

questions.stem: On arrival in Rome, Paul first addressed
questions.explanation: After three days he called together the local leaders of the Jews (Acts 28:17).

questions.stem: 'I heard the sound of thee in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; and I hid myself.' The question that immediately followed this statement was
options: 'What is this that you have done?'
'Who told you that you are naked?'
'Have you eaten of the tree of which I commanded you not to eat?'
questions.explanation: God replied, 'Who told you that you were naked?' and then asked about the tree (Gen. 3:10-11).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: One of the rules given to Noah after the flood was that he should
options: not eat flesh with its blood
questions.explanation: 'You shall not eat flesh with its life, that is, its blood' (Gen. 9:4).

questions.stem: '... Let peoples serve you, and nations bow down to you ...' This statement was made by
questions.explanation: Isaac said this when blessing Jacob (Gen. 27:29).

questions.stem: 'The lad is gone; and I, where shall I go?' Which of Joseph's brothers uttered these words?
questions.explanation: Reuben said this when he found Joseph gone from the pit (Gen. 37:29-30).

questions.stem: Pharaoh oppressed the Israelites because
options: he feared that they might join his enemies to fight him
they continued to give birth to male children
the midwives did not kill the children at birth
he did not know Jacob and Joseph
questions.explanation: 'Lest they multiply, and, if war befall us, they join our enemies and fight against us' (Ex. 1:10).

questions.stem: '... The Lord will fight for you, and you have only to be still.' The Lord fought for the people of Israel on the occasion referred to in the statement by
options: drowning the Egyptian army in the Red Sea
opening a chasm in the earth and swallowing their enemies
raining fire and brimstone on their enemies
raining hail and stones on their enemies
questions.explanation: Moses said this at the Red Sea, where the Egyptians were drowned (Ex. 14:13-14, 27-28).

questions.stem: When Moses delayed to come down from the mountain, the Israelites
options: decided to go back to Egypt
went up to look for him
asked Aaron to make gods for them
questions.explanation: 'Up, make us gods, who shall go before us' (Ex. 32:1).

questions.stem: Moses could not enter the Promised Land because he
options: was too old to cross the border
was too busy preparing his successor
did not give due regard to God
questions.explanation: 'Because you did not believe in me, to sanctify me in the eyes of the people of Israel' (Num. 20:12).

questions.stem: Moses consecrated Joshua as the new leader of Israel in the presence of
questions.explanation: Moses set Joshua before Eleazar the priest and the congregation (Num. 27:19-22).

questions.stem: 'All that you have commanded us we will do, and wherever you send us we will go. Just as we obeyed Moses in all things, so we will obey you ...' This pledge was made to Joshua by the
options: Reubenites, the Gadites and the half-tribe of Manasseh
questions.explanation: Joshua had just addressed the Reubenites, Gadites and half-tribe of Manasseh, and they answered with this pledge (Josh. 1:12-16).

questions.stem: Rahab the harlot assisted the Israelite spies as they prepared to attack
options: the five kings of the Amorites
questions.explanation: Rahab hid the spies sent to view Jericho (Josh. 2:1).

questions.stem: 'Out of the eater came something to eat. Out of the strong came something sweet.' This riddle was explained first to Samson's
questions.explanation: Samson said he had not told even his father and mother, but on the seventh day he told his wife (Judg. 14:16-17).

questions.stem: For offending God, the Israelites were delivered into the power of Midian for
questions.explanation: 'The Lord gave them into the hand of Midian seven years' (Judg. 6:1).

questions.stem: Gideon was able to defeat the Midianites with a reduced number of soldiers because he
questions.explanation: God reduced the army to 300 so that Israel would know the victory was the Lord's; Gideon trusted God (Judg. 7:2-22).

questions.stem: Elkanah would give Hannah only one portion of the sacrifice because
questions.explanation: 'Although he loved Hannah, he would give Hannah only one portion, because the Lord had closed her womb' (1 Sam. 1:5, RSV).

questions.stem: Who was unfaithful to her husband as Israel was to God?
questions.explanation: Hosea's wife Gomer symbolized unfaithful Israel (Hos. 1:2-3; 3:1).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: '... To your tents, O Israel!' This was a signal for
questions.explanation: With this cry the northern tribes rebelled against Rehoboam (1 Kings 12:16).

questions.stem: 'As the Lord the God of Israel lives, before whom I stand, there shall be neither dew nor rain these years, except by my word.' Who was the Israelite king during the period of the drought?
questions.explanation: Elijah said this to Ahab (1 Kings 17:1).

questions.stem: When Elisha received the message about Ben-hadad's ill-health, the prophet wept because
options: Ben-hadad would not recover from the sickness
Hazael would be cruel to Israel
questions.explanation: 'Because I know the evil that you will do to the people of Israel' (2 Kings 8:11-12).

questions.stem: '... Incline thy ear, O Lord, and hear; open thy eyes, O Lord, and see; and hear the words of Sennacherib, which he has sent to mock the living God ...' This was the prayer of
questions.explanation: Hezekiah prayed this in the temple (2 Kings 19:15-16).

questions.stem: '... Behold, I am bringing upon Jerusalem and Judah such evil that the ears of every one who hears of it will tingle ...' The above was said because of the sins of
questions.explanation: The Lord said this because Manasseh had committed abominations (2 Kings 21:11-12).

questions.stem: Saul initially desired to kill David because
options: David became very popular after killing Goliath
David married Michal and befriended Jonathan
Saul was tormented by an evil spirit
questions.explanation: The women's song, 'Saul has slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands', made Saul angry and jealous (1 Sam. 18:7-11).

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: God revealed to Solomon that the kingdom would be divided after him because he
questions.explanation: His heart turned after other gods, so the Lord said he would tear the kingdom from him (1 Kings 11:4-11).

questions.stem: 'In the year that King Uzziah died I saw the Lord sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up; and his train filled the temple.' Which prophet is associated with this vision?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 6:1.

questions.stem: King Herod granted the request of the daughter of Herodias by beheading John the Baptist because
options: the king was impressed by the way she danced
John the Baptist opposed the king's love affair with Herodias
Herod was bound by oath and personal integrity
Herod was anxious to see John the Baptist dead
questions.explanation: 'The king was exceedingly sorry; but because of his oaths and his guests he did not want to break his word' (Mark 6:26).

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a condition for being a disciple of Jesus?
options: Having a good knowledge of the scriptures
questions.explanation: Jesus demanded self-denial, taking up the cross and confessing him (Luke 9:23-26), not scriptural knowledge.

questions.stem: According to Mark's Gospel, the first miracle of Jesus was
options: opening the eyes of a blind man
healing a man with an unclean spirit
raising a dead boy to life
questions.explanation: Mark's first miracle is the healing of the man with an unclean spirit in the Capernaum synagogue (Mark 1:23-26).

questions.stem: When the disciples thought that the kingdom of God was to appear immediately, Jesus told them the parable of the
questions.explanation: 'Because they supposed that the kingdom of God was to appear immediately', he told the parable of the pounds (Luke 19:11-27).

questions.stem: The miracle which Jesus performed on the Sabbath was the healing of the
questions.explanation: He healed the man with the withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath (Mark 3:1-5).

questions.stem: Peacemakers are blessed because they shall
questions.explanation: 'Blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called sons of God' (Matt. 5:9).

questions.stem: 'He who hears you hears me, and he who rejects you rejects me ...' The above statement was addressed to
options: the twelve whom he sent out to preach
all the disciples, just before the Ascension
the seventy whom he sent out to preach
all the disciples during the Sermon on the Mount
questions.explanation: Jesus said this when sending out the seventy (Luke 10:1, 16).

questions.stem: 'A great prophet has arisen among us!' and 'God has visited his people!' These statements were made during the
options: raising of the son of the widow of Nain
questions.explanation: The crowd said this after Jesus raised the widow's son at Nain (Luke 7:11-16).

questions.stem: Jesus gave the sign of Jonah to the Pharisees to indicate his
options: three-fold office as Prophet, Priest and King
questions.explanation: 'As Jonah was three days and three nights in the belly of the whale, so will the Son of man be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth' (Matt. 12:40).

questions.stem: The Jews asked Jesus whether they should pay their tax or not because they wanted to
options: help him and his disciples to pay taxes
questions.explanation: They sent men 'to entrap him in his talk' (Mark 12:13).

questions.stem: Jesus began to teach his disciples about his suffering, rejection, crucifixion and resurrection after
questions.explanation: After Peter's confession 'he began to teach them that the Son of man must suffer many things' (Mark 8:29-31).

questions.stem: '... For the Son of man also came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.' This statement was made by Jesus
options: after healing two blind men near Jericho
immediately before he told the parable of the householder
during the discussion that followed the request of the sons of Zebedee
as he was foretelling his crucifixion and resurrection
questions.explanation: Jesus said this after the request of James and John (Mark 10:35-45).

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Herod (Lk. 23:6-12)
questions.stem: Herod was very glad to see Jesus at the trial because
options: John the Baptist spoke to him about Jesus
he believed that Jesus was the Messiah
he hoped to see Jesus perform some miracles
the quarrel between Herod and Pilate was settled on account of Jesus
questions.explanation: 'He was hoping to see some sign done by him' (Luke 23:8).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: 'Blessed is the King who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!' This verse is connected with
options: the song of the disciples after the Last Supper
questions.explanation: The disciples sang this at the triumphal entry (Luke 19:37-38).

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: According to Mark, the people who saw where Jesus was laid were Mary Magdalene and
questions.explanation: Mark 15:47 names Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses, who is the same Mary as 'the mother of James the younger and of Joses' (Mark 15:40).

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: The message of the risen Christ to the women who came early to the tomb was to be relayed to the disciples and to
questions.explanation: 'Go, tell his disciples and Peter that he is going before you to Galilee' (Mark 16:7).

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: 'I have no silver and gold, but I give you what I have; in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, walk.' This was said by Peter to a lame man
questions.explanation: The lame man lay at the gate of the temple called Beautiful (Acts 3:2-6).

questions.stem: The immediate cause of the stoning of Stephen was his
options: declaration of Jesus as the Righteous One
condemnation of the Jewish rite of circumcision
claim to see Jesus at the right hand of God
questions.explanation: When he said, 'I see... the Son of man standing at the right hand of God', they rushed upon him and stoned him (Acts 7:56-58).

questions.stem: 'But when they recognized that he was a Jew, for about two hours they all with one voice cried out, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"' Who was the Jew alluded to here?
questions.explanation: The Jews put Alexander forward, and the crowd shouted when they recognized he was a Jew (Acts 19:33-34).

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: Saul and Barnabas were sent on their mission by the
questions.explanation: The church at Antioch laid hands on them and sent them off (Acts 13:1-3).

questions.stem: 'They have beaten us publicly, uncondemned, men who are Roman citizens, and have thrown us into prison; and do they now cast us out secretly? ...' This experience of Paul was in
questions.explanation: Paul said this to the magistrates at Philippi (Acts 16:12, 37).

questions.stem: Paul purified himself in the Temple after the third missionary journey because he was
options: advised to do so by the elders
questions.explanation: The elders at Jerusalem told him to purify himself with the four men who were under a vow (Acts 21:23-26).

questions.stem: During Paul's trial before the Council, he brought about a division between the Pharisees and Sadducees by mentioning the issue of
questions.explanation: 'With respect to the hope and the resurrection of the dead I am on trial' (Acts 23:6-8).

questions.stem: On the island of Malta, Paul healed a man who was
questions.explanation: Publius' father lay sick with fever and dysentery, and Paul healed him (Acts 28:8).

questions.stem: 'Your blood be upon your heads! I am innocent. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.' The above statement was made by
questions.explanation: Paul said this to the Jews at Corinth (Acts 18:6).

questions.stem: What was upon the face of the deep on the first day of creation?
questions.explanation: Gen. 1:2 says darkness was upon the face of the deep before God said, 'Let there be light'.

questions.stem: "Let there be lights in the firmament of the heavens to separate the day from the night ..." This statement was made by God on the
questions.explanation: The sun, moon and stars were created on the fourth day (Gen. 1:14-19).

questions.stem: The story of the Fall teaches that
options: man was made in the image of God
it is a sin to disobey God
Adam was less guilty than Eve
questions.explanation: Adam and Eve disobeyed God's command not to eat of the tree, and sin and punishment followed (Gen. 3).

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: 'On that day all the fountains of the great deep burst forth and the windows of the heavens were opened.' The result of this was a
questions.explanation: Gen. 7:11-12: rain fell upon the earth forty days and forty nights.

questions.stem: "Who would have said to Abraham that Sarah would suckle children?..." Who said this?
questions.explanation: Sarah said these words at the birth of Isaac (Gen. 21:7).

questions.stem: The quotation, "Let me not look upon the death of the child" comes from the story about
options: the expulsion of Hagar and Ishmael
Moses when he was placed on the bank of the Nile
questions.explanation: Hagar said this in the wilderness of Beersheba after the water was spent (Gen. 21:16).

questions.stem: Joseph's dream about his future leadership of his brothers was fulfilled when he became
options: the second in command of Pharaoh
questions.explanation: As Pharaoh's second in command his brothers came and bowed before him (Gen. 41:40-43; 42:6).

questions.stem: The children of Israel cried out to God for help in Egypt because
options: Moses failed to look after them
questions.explanation: Ex. 2:23: the people groaned under their bondage and cried out for help.

questions.stem: "What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?" The above statement was made by
questions.explanation: Ex. 14:5: the mind of Pharaoh and his servants was changed and they said this.

questions.stem: The manna which the Israelites left till the morning in disobedience to God
questions.explanation: Ex. 16:20: it bred worms and became foul.

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: God gave the ten commandments to the people of Israel because He
options: wanted their days to be long
redeemed them from slavery in Egypt
frowned at those who took His Name in vain
questions.explanation: The commandments are prefaced, 'I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage' (Ex. 20:2).

questions.stem: "...Choose this day whom you will serve, ... as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD." The Israelites' response to the above statement is '...we
options: also will serve the LORD, for He is our God'
cannot serve the LORD, for He is a holy God'
will serve the LORD though He is a jealous God'
cannot put away the foreign gods among us because our fathers served them'
questions.explanation: Josh. 24:18: 'therefore we also will serve the LORD, for he is our God.'

questions.stem: God's anger was kindled against Eli and his children because Eli did not
options: train his children in the way of the LORD
apply appropriate sanctions on his children when due
know the gravity of their actions
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 3:13: his sons were blaspheming God and he did not restrain them.

questions.stem: The prophets whom Saul met at Gibeath-elohim as a confirmation that the LORD had anointed him to rule over God's people, were
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 10:5-10: a band of prophets came prophesying with instruments and Saul prophesied with them - ecstatic prophets.

questions.stem: While David was being anointed king, he received
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 16:13: the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon David from that day.

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: Against whom were the Israelites fighting when King David committed adultery with Uriah's wife?
questions.explanation: 2 Sam. 11:1: Joab and Israel ravaged the Ammonites and besieged Rabbah.

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: According to Psalm 51, the sacrifice acceptable to God is
questions.explanation: Ps. 51:17: 'The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit.'

questions.stem: Solomon could devote his attention to the building of the house of the LORD because
options: of the supplies from the Queen of Sheba
there was neither adversary nor misfortune
of David's purchase of the site for the building
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 5:4: 'the LORD my God has given me rest on every side; there is neither adversary nor misfortune.'

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: The immediate cause of the division of the kingdom was
questions.explanation: Rehoboam rejected the elders' counsel and threatened heavier yokes, so Israel rebelled (1 Kings 12:13-16).

questions.stem: "Arise go to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and dwell there. Behold, I have commanded a widow there to feed you". What exactly necessitated this event?
options: The drought caused by Elijah's curse
Ahab's evil in the sight of the LORD
The ravens ceased to feed Elijah
questions.explanation: The brook Cherith dried up because there was no rain in the land, the drought Elijah announced (1 Kings 17:1, 7-9).

questions.stem: "Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, ..." is a hymn of praise by
options: the Virgin Mary at the Annunciation
Zechariah at the birth of John the Baptist
Simeon at the presentation of Jesus in the Temple
Elizabeth at the visit of Mary
questions.explanation: The Benedictus was sung by Zechariah at John's birth (Lk. 1:67-68).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: According to the birth and infancy narratives in St. Matthew, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream three times. In the second appearance, he instructed Joseph to
options: accept that Mary was a virgin
questions.explanation: In the second dream Joseph was told to flee to Egypt (Mt. 2:13); the third told him to return (Mt. 2:19-20).

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: "Lord, now lettest thou thy servant depart in peace, according to thy word; for mine eyes have seen thy salvation ..." This was said at the dedication of Jesus by
questions.explanation: Simeon spoke the Nunc Dimittis in the Temple (Lk. 2:28-32).

questions.stem: "You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the wrath to come?" In Matthew's account, John the Baptist addressed this to the
questions.explanation: Mt. 3:7: he saw many Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism.

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: The second temptation of Jesus according to Luke's account of the gospel was
options: giving the kingdoms of the world to Jesus if he would worship the devil
a command for a stone to become bread
jumping down from the pinnacle of the temple
denying the name of God, the Father
questions.explanation: Luke's order is bread, the kingdoms of the world, then the pinnacle of the temple (Lk. 4:3-12).

questions.stem: What did Christ say should be the qualification of whoever was to be first or great among the apostles?
options: Giving one's life as a ransom
Drinking from the same cup as Jesus
questions.explanation: Mk. 10:44: 'whoever would be first among you must be slave of all.'

questions.stem: A would-be disciple, who puts his hand to the plough and looks back, lacks
questions.explanation: Lk. 9:62: such a person is not fit for the kingdom of God - he lacks total commitment.

questions.stem: In which miracle story was Jesus mistaken for a ghost by his disciples?
options: The feeding of the five thousand
Calming of the storm and sea
questions.explanation: When they saw him walking on the sea they thought it was a ghost (Mk. 6:49).

questions.stem: According to Luke, the healing of the paralytic was intended to show that
options: Jesus has authority to forgive sins
the Holy Spirit makes intercession for sinners
questions.explanation: Lk. 5:24: 'that you may know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins'.

questions.stem: The story of the healing of blind Bartimaeus teaches that
options: prayer is very basic to healing
there is need to persistently shout for attention
Jesus is the Son of David
faith is a pre-requisite to healing
questions.explanation: Jesus told him, 'Go your way; your faith has made you well' (Mk. 10:52).

questions.topic: Parables about love of God (Mt. 18:12-14; Lk. 15:1-32)
questions.stem: The parable of the prodigal son emphasizes that
options: it is not good for the son and the father to quarrel
the father loves the second son more than the first
questions.explanation: The son repents and returns and the father receives him back (Lk. 15:17-24).

questions.stem: According to Matthew's account of the gospel, the most important divine requirement for entering the kingdom of heaven is
questions.explanation: Mt. 7:21: only he who does the will of my Father who is in heaven will enter.

questions.stem: After their mission, the seventy disciples reported to Jesus that
options: they enjoyed the hospitality of people
demons were subject to them in His name
questions.explanation: Lk. 10:17: 'Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!'

questions.stem: The appearance of Moses and Elijah at the transfiguration underscores the importance in the ministry of Jesus of
questions.explanation: Moses represents the law and Elijah the prophets, both fulfilled in Jesus.

questions.stem: "This is my beloved Son; listen to him". This was said on the occasion of Jesus'
questions.explanation: The voice from the cloud said this at the transfiguration (Mk. 9:7).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: "...My house shall be a house of prayer; but you have made it a den of robbers". Just before making this statement, the speaker
options: drove out those who sold in the temple
questions.explanation: Jesus drove out those who sold and bought in the temple and then said this (Mt. 21:12-13).

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
questions.stem: Which of the following questions did the high priest ask Jesus during His trial?
options: 'Are you the Christ, the son of the Blessed?'
'Are you the King of the Jews?'
questions.explanation: Mk. 14:61: the high priest asked, 'Are you the Christ, the Son of the Blessed?' ('King of the Jews' was Pilate's question).

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: "...Do not weep for me, but weep for yourselves and for your children..." These words were addressed by Jesus to the
questions.explanation: Lk. 23:28: 'Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me...'

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: What was the first statement of Jesus on the cross according to Luke's account of the gospel?
options: 'Today you shall be with me in paradise.'
'Father forgive them for they do not know what they do.'
questions.explanation: In Luke, the first word is 'Father, forgive them' (Lk. 23:34), before the word to the penitent thief (23:43).

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: Very early in the morning, on the first day of the week, three women went to the tomb of Jesus to
options: see whether the soldiers had carried the body away
questions.explanation: Mk. 16:1: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Salome bought spices to anoint him.

questions.stem: "...Let all the house of Israel therefore know assuredly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified..." As a reaction to this declaration, the Jews
options: decided to kill Peter and the apostles
went back to their houses in anger
were deeply troubled and asked what they should do
questions.explanation: Acts 2:37: they were cut to the heart and asked, 'Brethren, what shall we do?'

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: "...You have not lied to men but to God". The immediate effect of this statement of Peter on the liar was that he
questions.explanation: Acts 5:5: Ananias fell down and died.

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: The apostles created a new office in the ministry besides prayer and preaching, in order to address the problems of
questions.explanation: The seven were appointed because the Hellenists' widows were being neglected in the daily distribution (Acts 6:1-6).

questions.stem: Saul's encounter with the Risen Christ on the road to Damascus convinced him that
options: Jesus is the Son of God
the faith of his father was right
he should have gone to Damascus with more armed escort
questions.explanation: Immediately afterwards he proclaimed Jesus in the synagogues, saying, 'He is the Son of God' (Acts 9:20).

questions.stem: When Saul escaped from Damascus to Jerusalem after his conversion, the disciples in Jerusalem
options: were full of sympathy for him
questions.explanation: Acts 9:26: they were all afraid of him, not believing he was a disciple.

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: Paul and Barnabas were referred to as 'gods' in Lystra because they
options: were agents of the unknown God
questions.explanation: After Paul healed the man crippled from birth, the crowd said, 'The gods have come down to us' (Acts 14:8-11).

questions.stem: "... Abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from unchastity..." To which issue was the above a response?
questions.explanation: This was the decision of the Council of Jerusalem on whether Gentile converts must be circumcised (Acts 15:1, 28-29).

questions.stem: "... I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; with respect to the hope and resurrection of the dead I am on trial." This was part of the address of Paul to
questions.explanation: Paul said this before the council (Sanhedrin) in Acts 23:6.

questions.topic: Love for one another (Jn. 13:34-35; 15:12-13; cf. 1 Jn. 4:7-21; 1 Cor. 13)
questions.stem: According to Paul, which of the following is the greatest?
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 13:13: faith, hope, love abide, but the greatest of these is love.

questions.stem: According to the creation account of Genesis 1, God charged man to
options: have dominion over all the earth
questions.explanation: Gen. 1:26-28: God told man to fill the earth, subdue it and have dominion.

questions.stem: When God told Abraham that Sarah would have a child, Abraham laughed because
options: they were too old to have a child
he already had a child called Ishmael
questions.explanation: Gen. 17:17: 'Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety, bear a child?'

questions.stem: After Jacob's dream at Bethel, he promised that he would
options: give a tenth of all he would have to God
return immediately and settle there with his family
go to his father's house in peace
questions.explanation: Gen. 28:22: 'of all that thou givest me I will give the tenth to thee.'

questions.stem: Why did God redeem the Israelites from the hands of Pharaoh?
options: God remembered His covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
The yoke of the Israelites was heavy
God wanted to show His power to Pharaoh
He wanted to show that Moses was powerful
questions.explanation: Ex. 2:24: God heard their groaning and remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

questions.stem: When the people of Israel saw the great work of the LORD in drowning the Egyptians, they
options: built an altar to the LORD
questions.explanation: Ex. 14:31: the people feared the LORD and believed in the LORD and in his servant Moses.

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: During the giving of the law at Mount Sinai, the Israelites wanted Moses to speak to them instead of God because
options: the people were afraid and trembled
questions.explanation: Ex. 20:19: 'You speak to us, and we will hear; but let not God speak to us, lest we die.'

questions.stem: Where did Joshua gather all the tribes of Israel for presentation before God?
questions.explanation: Josh. 24:1: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem.

questions.stem: The valley of Eshcol is symbolic to Israel because it was the place where
options: Moses and his people had a resounding victory over the Amalekites
the men of Israel cut down the cluster of grapes
the spies set out to survey Canaan
the Israelites challenged the leadership of Moses and Aaron
questions.explanation: Num. 13:23-24: the spies cut down a cluster of grapes there, hence the name Eshcol.

questions.stem: The Shema emphasizes the
options: importance of Israel to the world
questions.explanation: Deut. 6:4: 'Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD.'

questions.stem: "The LORD give you children by this woman for the loan which she lent to the LORD;..." The 'loan' referred to in this blessing is
questions.explanation: Eli blessed Elkanah and Hannah after she dedicated Samuel to the LORD (1 Sam. 2:20).

questions.stem: A good example of parental upbringing is manifested in the son of
questions.explanation: Samuel's, Eli's and David's sons went astray, but Jehoshaphat son of Asa 'walked in all the way of Asa his father' (1 Kings 22:43).

questions.stem: The leadership potential of David was demonstrated publicly for the first time when he
options: spared King Saul's life in the cave
questions.explanation: His victory over Goliath before both armies was the first public display of his leadership (1 Sam. 17).

questions.topic: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
questions.stem: Although David refused to kill Saul because he was the LORD'S anointed, he still believed that
options: Saul would be killed by the Philistines
the LORD would eventually smite Saul
Saul's soldiers would cause him to die in battle
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 26:10: 'the LORD will smite him; or his day shall come to die; or he shall go down into battle.'

questions.topic: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
questions.stem: "Blessed be you, my son David! You will do many things and will succeed in them", the above statement was made when David
questions.explanation: Saul said this after David spared his life in the wilderness of Ziph (1 Sam. 26:25).

questions.stem: Solomon asked God for wisdom to enable him
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:9: 'an understanding mind to govern thy people, that I may discern between good and evil'.

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: The consequence of Rehoboam's unwise decision at the time the Israelites came to him at Shechem eventually resulted in
questions.explanation: Israel rebelled against the house of David and made Jeroboam king (1 Kings 12:16-20).

questions.stem: The new covenant which God was to make with the house of Israel was that it would be
options: for the tribe of Judah alone
questions.explanation: Jer. 31:33: 'I will put my law within them, and I will write it upon their hearts.'

questions.topic: The birth and boyhood of Jesus (Mt. 1:18-25; 2; Lk. 1:26-45; 2)
questions.stem: "Go and search diligently for the child, and when you have found him bring me word,..." The intention of the speaker in this context was to
options: pay homage to the Lord Jesus
kill all the children in the area
questions.explanation: Herod pretended he wished to worship, but he sought to destroy the child (Mt. 2:8, 13).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: Jesus was tempted in the wilderness in order to
options: prove that He was the Son of God
prepare Him for His earthly ministry
questions.explanation: The temptation immediately preceded and prepared Jesus for his public ministry (Lk. 4:14).

questions.stem: One important fact about Mary brought out in Jesus' miracle of changing water to wine was that she
options: must intercede for a miracle to occur
was a sister of the bridegroom
had a deep insight of her son and His ability
questions.explanation: She told the servants, 'Do whatever he tells you' (Jn. 2:5), showing trust in his power.

questions.stem: The raising of Lazarus illustrates that Jesus
options: was a good friend of Lazarus
questions.explanation: Jesus said, 'I am the resurrection and the life' and raised Lazarus (Jn. 11:25, 43-44).

questions.stem: "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof, ..." The continuation of this message by the centurion indicated that
options: he had faith in the power of Jesus' word
as a Gentile, he did not like the Jews
as an army officer, he wanted to avoid contact with Jesus
questions.explanation: He continued, 'say the word, and let my servant be healed' (Lk. 7:6-7).

questions.stem: The epileptic boy could not be healed by the disciples because
options: they had not yet received power
their prayers were not intensive enough
they had to wait for Jesus
questions.explanation: Mk. 9:29: 'This kind cannot be driven out by anything but prayer.'

questions.stem: Based on the Sermon on the Plain: the poor in spirit are promised
questions.explanation: Lk. 6:20: 'Blessed are you poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.'

questions.stem: Based on the Sermon on the Plain: those that are hated and reviled shall
options: have a great reward in heaven
questions.explanation: Lk. 6:22-23: 'your reward is great in heaven.'

questions.topic: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)
questions.stem: Jesus' objective for sending out the twelve was
options: for them to teach the Gentiles about the God of the Jews
to train the disciples in His ministry
to demonstrate that He was about to be crucified
to divert the attention of Herod from Himself
questions.explanation: He gave them power and sent them to preach and heal as he did, training them for his ministry (Lk. 9:1-2).

questions.stem: Who appeared and talked with Jesus during the transfiguration?
questions.explanation: Mk. 9:4: Elijah with Moses appeared and talked with Jesus.

questions.stem: "Grant us to sit, one at your right hand and one at your left, in your glory..." Why was this request by the sons of Zebedee not granted?
options: They were not qualified for the privilege
The other disciples disagreed with them
They were unable to drink the cup
It was not the duty of Jesus to grant their request
questions.explanation: Mk. 10:40: 'to sit at my right hand or at my left is not mine to grant'.

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: Where did Jesus lodge after he cleansed the temple?
questions.explanation: Mt. 21:17: he went out of the city to Bethany and lodged there.

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: At the trials of Jesus, Pilate was perplexed because
options: the Jews had no genuine case against Him
Jesus gave no answer to the charges
the Jews asked for the release of Barabbas, a notorious criminal
he knew that Jesus had performed many miracles among the Jews
questions.explanation: Mk. 15:5: Jesus made no further answer, so that Pilate wondered.

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: Why did the accusers of Jesus stay behind while He was led to the Praetorium?
options: It was forbidden to follow the accused
They did not want to be defiled
questions.explanation: Jn. 18:28: they did not enter, so that they might not be defiled but might eat the passover.

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: Who was forced to carry the cross behind Jesus?
questions.explanation: Lk. 23:26: they seized Simon of Cyrene and laid the cross on him.

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: "Truly I say to you, today you will be with me in Paradise". Jesus said this to
questions.explanation: Lk. 23:43: said to the criminal who asked to be remembered.

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: According to Luke, the people who first got to Jesus' tomb were
options: Mary the mother of Jesus, Peter and John
Mary Magdalene and the other women
questions.explanation: Lk. 24:1, 10: Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary the mother of James and the other women.

questions.topic: The Door, the Lamb and the Good Shepherd (Jn. 1:29-34; 10:1-18)
questions.stem: Jesus Christ, the Good Shepherd was loved by the Father because He
options: understood the needs of the sheep
laid down His life for the sheep
questions.explanation: Jn. 10:17: 'For this reason the Father loves me, because I lay down my life.'

questions.stem: Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life: he who believes in me, though he die, yet shall he live, and whoever lives and believes in me shall never die..." On what occasion was this statement made?
options: On the day of Jesus' resurrection
When Jesus demonstrated the fact of His resurrection to Thomas
On the day Jesus restored Lazarus back to life
When Jairus' daughter was raised from the dead
questions.explanation: Jesus said this to Martha before raising Lazarus (Jn. 11:25-26).

questions.topic: Love for one another (Jn. 13:34-35; 15:12-13; cf. 1 Jn. 4:7-21; 1 Cor. 13)
questions.stem: According to Paul, if we give away all that we have and we deliver our bodies to be burned, but have not love we
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 13:3: '...but have not love, I gain nothing.'

questions.stem: "Now the company of those who believed were of one heart and soul..." This reveals that the early Christians
options: were always filled with the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 4:32: no one said any of his things was his own; they had everything in common.

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: The suggestion to choose the seven deacons was made by
questions.explanation: Acts 6:2-3: the twelve summoned the disciples and told them to pick seven men.

questions.stem: "And in the last days it shall be, God declares, that I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions..." This prophecy was fulfilled
questions.explanation: Peter quoted Joel at Pentecost to explain the outpouring of the Spirit (Acts 2:16-17).

questions.stem: Who was sent by God to restore Saul's sight after his encounter with Jesus on the road to Damascus?
questions.explanation: Acts 9:17-18: Ananias laid his hands on him and he regained his sight.

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them". This statement was made by the
questions.explanation: Acts 13:2: the Holy Spirit said this at Antioch.

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: Following his encounter with the apostles, the ruler of Cyprus
options: became blind for resisting the gospel
requested that they choose another time to preach the gospel
questions.explanation: Sergius Paulus believed when he saw what happened to Elymas (Acts 13:12); it was Elymas who became blind.

questions.stem: When Elijah escaped to the brook Cherith, he was fed by
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 17:6: the ravens brought him bread and meat.

questions.stem: The contest on Mount Carmel was to prove that
options: Baal was the god of Israel
God was supreme to other gods
questions.explanation: The fire from the LORD showed that the LORD is God (1 Kings 18:24, 39).

questions.stem: Naboth did not agree to release his vineyard to Ahab because
options: the amount offered for it was too small
it was his major source of income
it was the inheritance of his fathers
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:3: 'The LORD forbid that I should give you the inheritance of my fathers.'

questions.stem: What did Gehazi deceitfully receive from Naaman?
options: two talents of silver and two festal garments
two talents of silver and two shekels of gold
two festal garments and two talents of gold
two thousand shekels and two festal garments
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:23: Naaman tied up two talents of silver with two festal garments.

questions.stem: The greatest achievement of King Josiah of Judah was his
options: sweeping reforms of the religious life of his people
training a worthy successor before his death
questions.explanation: Josiah renewed the covenant and purged idolatry throughout Judah (2 Kings 23).

questions.stem: Jerusalem fell in 586 B.C. to the Babylonian King called
questions.explanation: Nebuchadnezzar's army destroyed Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:1-10).

questions.topic: Response to the state of Judah (Neh. 2; 4:1-23; Ezra 3:4; 5; 6; 7)
questions.stem: And the King (Artaxerxes) said to me, "Why is your face sad, seeing you are not sick? This is nothing else but sadness of the heart" Why was the addressee sad?
options: The condition of Jerusalem was deplorable
He was fasting because of Jerusalem
Enemies of Jerusalem were laughing at him
He was in exile in Babylon
questions.explanation: Neh. 2:3: the city of his fathers lay waste and its gates were destroyed by fire.

questions.stem: Although Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego were cast into the fiery furnace, King Nebuchadnezzar was astonished to see four men in the furnace. He said the fourth man was like
questions.explanation: Dan. 3:25 (RSV): 'the appearance of the fourth is like a son of the gods.'

questions.stem: In the belly of the fish Jonah prayed to God to
questions.explanation: Jonah's prayer (Jonah 2) is a cry from distress for deliverance: 'I called to the LORD, out of my distress, and he answered me.'

questions.stem: Daniel was distinguished above all other satraps and presidents because he
options: had an excellent spirit in him
refused to worship the golden image
questions.explanation: Dan. 6:3: an excellent spirit was in him.

questions.stem: Daniel could not be harmed by the lions because
options: an angel shut the mouths of the lions
a pillar of cloud separated Daniel from the lions
questions.explanation: Dan. 6:22: 'My God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths.'

questions.stem: The Israelites did evil in the eyes of the LORD in the days of the Judges by
questions.explanation: Judg. 2:11: the people of Israel did evil and served the Baals.

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: 'Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Israel and for four, I will not revoke the punishment..."'. In the latter part of this prophecy, Amos condemned Israel for
options: not remembering the covenant of brotherhood
rejecting the laws and statutes of the LORD
questions.explanation: Amos 2:6-8 condemns selling the righteous for silver, trampling the poor and perverting justice; the other charges were against Tyre, Damascus/Ammon and Judah.

questions.stem: "Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then I said, 'Here am I! Send me.'" Why did Isaiah offer himself to be God's messenger?
options: Because the king had died and he needed another job
Having been cleansed of his sins, he saw the need to warn others
Because he had seen the beauty of heaven and wanted to work for God
questions.explanation: After his lips were touched with the burning coal and his sin forgiven, he volunteered (Is. 6:6-8).

questions.stem: Who, according to Ezekiel, did the exiles blame for their plight?
questions.explanation: Ezek. 18:2: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.'

questions.stem: God told Jeremiah that He would give Jerusalem into the hands of the Chaldeans because the Israelites
options: did not prepare adequately for war
questions.explanation: Jer. 32:28-32: because of all the evil they did to provoke me to anger.

questions.stem: The expression 'dry bones' in Ezekiel refers to
questions.explanation: Ezek. 37:11: 'these bones are the whole house of Israel.'

questions.stem: According to Paul, the law and the prophets bear witness to the
questions.explanation: Rom. 3:21: the righteousness of God has been manifested, the law and the prophets bearing witness to it.

questions.stem: According to Paul in his Letter to the Galatians, one is justified by
questions.explanation: Gal. 2:16: a man is not justified by works of the law but through faith in Jesus Christ.

questions.stem: The function of the law to believers before the coming of Christ was that of a
questions.explanation: Gal. 3:24 (RSV): 'the law was our custodian until Christ came.'

questions.stem: Justification by grace shows that work is
questions.explanation: Salvation is by grace through faith, not because of works (Rom. 3:24; Eph. 2:8-9).

questions.stem: All Christians who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized
questions.explanation: Rom. 6:3: all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death.

questions.stem: In what way did God condemn sin in the flesh?
options: He allowed Jesus to be crucified
Repentance was made possible for the forgiveness of sin
Resurrection of the flesh rendered sin ineffective
He sent His own Son in the likeness of man
questions.explanation: Rom. 8:3: sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, he condemned sin in the flesh.

questions.topic: Preparation for His coming (1 Thess. 5:1-11; 2 Pet. 3:1-13; Matt. 25:31-46)
questions.stem: 'But you are not in darkness brethren, for that day to surprise you like a thief.' That 'day' refers to the
questions.explanation: 1 Thess. 5:2-4 speaks of the day of the Lord coming like a thief in the night.

questions.stem: The main aim of the teaching of Christ's humility in Paul's Letter to the Philippians is that every Christian should
options: regard himself as equal to Jesus because He came in human form
confess that Jesus Christ is LORD to the glory of God the Father
work out his own salvation with fear and trembling
look into the interest of others and do nothing from selfishness
questions.explanation: Phil. 2:3-5: do nothing from selfishness; look to the interests of others; have this mind which was in Christ.

questions.stem: According to Paul's Letter to the Philippians, God exalted Jesus and gave Him a name which is above all names because He
options: was humble and obedient unto death
was the greatest man ever born
