questions.explanation: Phil. 2:8-9: he humbled himself and became obedient unto death; therefore God highly exalted him.

questions.stem: In the Letter to the Galatians, Christians are encouraged to bear one another's burdens in order to
questions.explanation: Gal. 6:2: 'Bear one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.'

questions.stem: 'Be angry but do not sin' means that anger
options: is not a sin at all
could be an occasion for sin
questions.explanation: Eph. 4:26-27: anger must not be allowed to lead to sin or give opportunity to the devil.

questions.stem: There are varieties of gifts and so different people have different gifts. Who gives all these gifts?
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 12:4, 11: there are varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit.

questions.stem: For the administration of the churches, Paul directed that Christians should
options: surrender all they have to the church
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 16:2: on the first day of every week each should put something aside.

questions.stem: Contribution of relief materials for the needy in the church according to Paul, must be
questions.explanation: 2 Cor. 9:7: God loves a cheerful giver.

questions.stem: Paul teaches that we should obey governing authorities in order to avoid
options: God's wrath and a bad conscience
questions.explanation: Rom. 13:5: be subject not only to avoid God's wrath but also for the sake of conscience.

questions.stem: When Paul says if anyone will not work, let him not eat, he is saying that
options: the lazy person must eat only a little
everyone should toil and labour with his hands
every person should seek lucrative job
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 3:8-12: Paul himself toiled and laboured, and commands all to work quietly and earn their own living.

questions.stem: Paul worked harder than any of the apostles because
options: he had the strength to do so
of the grace of God that was with him
Jesus personally revealed Himself to him
he was formerly a persecutor of the church
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 15:10: 'I worked harder than any of them, though it was not I, but the grace of God which is with me.'

questions.topic: Relationship in the Christian family (Eph. 6:1-9; Col. 3:18-21; 1 Pet. 3:1-7)
questions.stem: Christian wives are to be subject to their husbands
options: since their husbands take care of them
because it is fitting in the LORD
because it is the natural thing to do
since women are not expected to be heard
questions.explanation: Col. 3:18: 'Wives, be subject to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord.'

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: On being revealed at the coming of Christ, the lawless will be slain by the
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 2:8: the Lord Jesus will slay him with the breath of his mouth.

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: An important feature of the second coming of Jesus as taught by Paul is the
options: establishment of a world government under Christ
questions.explanation: 1 Thess. 4:16: the dead in Christ will rise first. (The lawless one is revealed before the coming and is destroyed by it.)

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: 'What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.' This statement refers to the
options: good works which are expected of the Christian
reward of the works of Christians
questions.explanation: Paul uses the seed image in 1 Cor. 15:35-44 to explain the resurrection of the dead.

questions.stem: Paul's experience as recorded in his second Letter to the Corinthians, teaches that the attitude of Christians to suffering should be that of
questions.explanation: Paul endured imprisonments, beatings and dangers without giving up (2 Cor. 11:23-33).

questions.topic: Obedience and Rewards: Abraham (Gen. 22:1-19), the three Hebrew youths (Dan. 3:1-30), David (1 Sam. 30:1-20)
questions.stem: Abraham's faith and works were better illustrated when he
options: took Lot with him to Canaan
offered his son, Isaac, on the altar
questions.explanation: Jas. 2:21-22: Abraham was justified by works when he offered Isaac; faith was active along with his works.

questions.stem: 'Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for ... For by it the men of old received divine approval.' Who are the men of old mentioned as examples of faith in the Letter to the Hebrews?
questions.explanation: Hebrews 11 lists Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Moses, Rahab and others.

questions.stem: According to James, effective prayer is that which is offered
questions.explanation: Jas. 5:15: the prayer of faith will save the sick man (cf. 1:6, ask in faith).

questions.topic: Christians living among non-Christians (1 Pet. 2:3-25; Rom. 15:1-2)
questions.stem: According to Peter, Christians living among non-Christians should
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 2:12: maintain good conduct among the Gentiles. (Printed 'condition' in the source.)

questions.stem: Peter enjoins Christians to be good citizens by
options: using their freedom to fight for their right
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 2:13-14: be subject for the Lord's sake to every human institution.

questions.stem: "Let us make man in our image..." In the statement above, 'man' refers to
questions.explanation: Gen. 1:27: in the image of God he created him; male and female he created them.

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: In the covenant with Noah, God equates blood with
questions.explanation: Gen. 9:4: flesh with its life, that is, its blood.

questions.stem: The covenant with Abraham stipulates that an uncircumcised male shall
options: find it difficult to have a child
be cut off from his people
questions.explanation: Gen. 17:14: any uncircumcised male shall be cut off from his people.

questions.stem: Joseph was hated the more by his brothers because
options: he was the first son of Rebecca
his father bought him a coat of many colours
questions.explanation: Gen. 37:5, 8: they hated him yet more for his dreams and for his words.

questions.stem: Pharaoh set Joseph over all the land of Egypt because he was
questions.explanation: Gen. 41:39-41: 'there is none so discreet and wise as you.'

questions.stem: In the burning bush, God revealed Himself to Moses as the God of
questions.explanation: Ex. 3:7-8: 'I have come down to deliver them out of the hand of the Egyptians.'

questions.stem: When the Hebrews left Egypt, God did not lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines because
options: He did not want them to see war and return to Egypt
He wanted to test their faith
the Hebrews went out of Egypt not equipped for war
questions.explanation: Ex. 13:17: 'Lest the people repent when they see war, and return to Egypt.'

questions.stem: Samuel's reaction during his first encounter with God showed that he was
options: afraid of the voice he heard
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 3:7: Samuel did not yet know the LORD, so he ran to Eli three times.

questions.stem: From the accounts in the First Book of Samuel, Eli's attitude to his children showed parental
questions.explanation: Eli rebuked his sons weakly and did not restrain them (1 Sam. 2:22-25; 3:13).

questions.topic: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
questions.stem: David demonstrated his submission to the will of God when he
options: lamented the death of Saul and Jonathan
questions.explanation: He stopped Abishai from killing the LORD's anointed (1 Sam. 26:9-11).

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: When David repented of his adultery with Bathsheba, he said,
options: "The man who has done this deserves to die..."
questions.explanation: 2 Sam. 12:13: David said to Nathan, 'I have sinned against the LORD.'

questions.stem: "The Lord has set the sun in the heavens, but has said that he would dwell in thick darkness..." This statement was made at the
questions.explanation: Solomon said this at the dedication of the temple (1 Kings 8:12).

questions.stem: In the first three chapters of the Book of Hosea, his main teaching is that
options: God loves us despite our sins
one should keep the commandments of God
questions.explanation: Hosea's love for unfaithful Gomer pictures God's love for unfaithful Israel (Hos. 3:1).

questions.stem: The valley of Achor in the Book of Hosea is a door of
questions.explanation: Hos. 2:15: 'make the Valley of Achor a door of hope.'

questions.stem: "Come, let us return to the Lord; for he has torn, that he may heal us; he has stricken, and he will bind us up." This call is to encourage
options: response to the need of the nation
questions.explanation: Hos. 6:1 calls Israel to return to the God who loves and heals them.

questions.stem: With reference to prophet Isaiah's vision, which of the following attributes must a minister of God possess?
questions.explanation: Isaiah saw the thrice-holy God and had to be cleansed before being sent (Is. 6:3-7).

questions.stem: What did God give to Ezekiel to eat in his vision?
questions.explanation: Ezek. 3:1-3: 'eat this scroll'.

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: Jesus was baptized by John the Baptist
options: to fulfil the prophecy about Him
so that the heavens could open up blessings for all believers
so that the Holy Spirit could descend upon Him
questions.explanation: Mt. 3:15: 'thus it is fitting for us to fulfil all righteousness.'

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: "Thou art my beloved Son; with thee I am well pleased." This statement was made during the
questions.explanation: The voice from heaven at Jesus' baptism (Mk. 1:11; Lk. 3:22).

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: According to the temptation narratives in the gospels according to Matthew and Luke, Jesus overcame Satan because He
options: depended on the word of God
questions.explanation: Each temptation was answered with 'It is written...' (Mt. 4:4, 7, 10).

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: "Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?" On what occasion was this question asked?
options: When Jesus ate in the house of Zacchaeus
Following the invitation of Jesus to a meal by a Pharisee
questions.explanation: Mt. 9:9-11: after Matthew's call, Jesus ate with tax collectors and the Pharisees asked this.

questions.stem: "Follow me and leave the dead to bury their own dead". By this statement, Jesus means that
options: there is no life after death
following Him comes before anything else
disciples should leave their families in God's care
questions.explanation: Mt. 8:22: discipleship takes priority over every other duty.

questions.stem: The disciples became terrified when they saw Jesus walking on the sea because
options: they thought He was a ghost
there was great storm in the sea
questions.explanation: Mt. 14:26: they were terrified, saying, 'It is a ghost!'

questions.stem: By the miracle of raising Lazarus to life, Jesus wanted to
options: reward Mary and Martha for their charity
convince the people that He was the LORD of life
questions.explanation: Jesus declared 'I am the resurrection and the life' and acted so that the people might believe (Jn. 11:25, 42).

questions.stem: The Jews sought all the more to kill Jesus after the healing of the man at the pool of Bethzatha because they thought that He
options: claimed to have authority to forgive sins
did not agree with the law of Moses
said that He was born before Abraham
questions.explanation: Jn. 5:18: he called God his Father, making himself equal with God.

questions.stem: In the gospel according to Matthew, the disciples could not heal the epileptic boy because
options: the boy's father had no faith in them
questions.explanation: Mt. 17:20: 'Because of your little faith.'

questions.stem: In the parable of the sower, the seed which fell on rocky ground refers to people whose conversion is
questions.explanation: They receive the word with joy but have no root and fall away (Mk. 4:16-17).

questions.topic: Parables about love of God (Mt. 18:12-14; Lk. 15:1-32)
questions.stem: The parable of the lost sheep teaches much about God's
questions.explanation: The shepherd seeks the one lost sheep; it is a parable of God's love for the lost (Lk. 15:4-7).

questions.stem: Turning the other cheek as preached by Jesus, implies that believers should
questions.explanation: Mt. 5:39: 'Do not resist one who is evil' - no retaliation.

questions.topic: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)
questions.stem: According to Matthew's account of the gospel, Jesus charged the twelve disciples to give without pay because they themselves
questions.explanation: Mt. 10:8: 'You received without pay, give without pay.'

questions.stem: Which disciples were with Jesus during the transfiguration?
questions.explanation: Mk. 9:2: Jesus took Peter, James and John.

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: Jesus wept over Jerusalem because
options: the people did not believe in Him
the city did not know the things that made for peace
people were buying and selling in the temple
the Pharisees and the priests had misled the people
questions.explanation: Lk. 19:41-42: 'Would that even today you knew the things that make for peace!'

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: In the Gospel according to Luke, the multitude that followed Jesus during the triumphal entry rejoiced and praised God with a loud voice because
options: they realized that Jesus was a prophet from Nazareth
of the mighty works that they had seen done by Jesus
Jesus was for the first time riding on a colt
they believed that Jesus would deliver them from the hands of their enemies
questions.explanation: Lk. 19:37: they praised God for all the mighty works that they had seen.

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
questions.stem: Jesus did not appeal to His Father for legions of angels to fight for Him because
options: it was not proper for angels to physically fight human beings
He could, on His own, avoid the cross
He wanted the scriptures to be fulfilled
the disciples were watching and praying
questions.explanation: Mt. 26:53-54: 'How then should the scriptures be fulfilled, that it must be so?'

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Herod (Lk. 23:6-12)
questions.stem: What did Pilate achieve by sending Jesus to Herod?
options: He escaped the anger of the Jews
Jesus was not killed in his hands
He was able to pacify the Jews
questions.explanation: Lk. 23:12: Herod and Pilate became friends that very day.

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: Which of Jesus' words on the cross led a bystander to give him vinegar?
options: "Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do."
"Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit."
"My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me"
questions.explanation: Mk. 15:34-36: hearing 'Eloi, Eloi...', a bystander ran, filled a sponge with vinegar and gave it to him.

questions.stem: When Jesus said that Lazarus would rise again, Martha thought that
options: Jesus would raise her brother from the dead
her brother would rise again at the last day
Jesus was talking of his own resurrection
He was talking of spiritual resurrection
questions.explanation: Jn. 11:24: 'I know that he will rise again in the resurrection at the last day.'

questions.stem: What kind of a man was elected to replace Judas Iscariot?
options: An opponent of the religious leaders
questions.explanation: Acts 1:21-22: one who accompanied them must become with us a witness to his resurrection.

questions.stem: The event of the day of Pentecost was prophesied by
questions.explanation: Acts 2:16: 'this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel.'

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: Who was the second martyr of the early church?
questions.explanation: After Stephen, Herod killed James the brother of John with the sword (Acts 12:2).

questions.stem: The Christian concept of Justification is that
options: through faith in Jesus the sinner is now regarded by God as guiltless
by one's efforts in keeping the law, man is now perfect before God
through his own knowledge, man can now do what is pleasing to God
by his natural wisdom, a sinner could be reconciled to God
questions.explanation: Rom. 3:22-24; 5:1: justified by faith, we have peace with God.

questions.stem: According to Paul, those who rely on the works of the law are under a curse since
options: the law is made for the weak
none can fully keep the law
the works of the law are of the devil
questions.explanation: Gal. 3:10: cursed be every one who does not abide by all things written in the law.

questions.stem: According to the Letter of Paul to the Romans, sin reigned in death, while grace reigned through righteousness to
questions.explanation: Rom. 5:21: grace reigns through righteousness to eternal life.

questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.stem: Christians believe that they are children of God because
options: they keep the laws and covenants of Abraham as commanded by God
they are church goers and benefactors
they are descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
through faith, they were baptized into Christ and put on Christ
questions.explanation: Gal. 3:26-27: in Christ you are all sons of God through faith; you have put on Christ.

questions.stem: Christians ought to be humble because
options: only the humble will inherit eternal life
questions.explanation: Phil. 2:5-8: have this mind which was in Christ, who humbled himself.

questions.stem: According to Paul, spiritual gifts, if properly employed, help in
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 14:12, 26: let all things be done for edification.

questions.stem: Paul advised Christians in Thessalonica to keep away from any brother who is
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 3:6: keep away from any brother who is living in idleness.

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: The order of events at the second coming of Christ will be that
options: those who are alive will be caught up first before the dead will rise
the dead will rise first before the living are caught up
the dead and the living will be caught up together
only the dead will rise leaving behind those who are alive
questions.explanation: 1 Thess. 4:16-17: the dead in Christ will rise first; then we who are alive shall be caught up.

questions.stem: Which of the following commandments is described by James as the royal law?
options: You shall have no other gods before me
You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart
You shall love your neighbour as yourself
You shall not covet your neighbour's property
questions.explanation: Jas. 2:8: the royal law, 'You shall love your neighbour as yourself.'

questions.stem: In extolling the sovereignty of God, Amos contrasted Him with the Nile, which he described as
options: the source of the waters of the sea
questions.explanation: Amos 8:8 and 9:5 describe the land rising like the Nile and sinking again like the Nile of Egypt at God's touch.

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: By keeping God’s covenant, the people of Israel would become
options: a kingdom of priests to God
a nation where God would manifest Himself
questions.explanation: Ex. 19:5-6: if Israel kept the covenant they would be God's own possession, a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.

questions.stem: Joseph saw his rise to leadership position in Egypt in relation to his brothers as
options: a proof of his superiority over them
an opportunity to avenge their evil deeds
a time to test their honesty
a means of preserving their lives
questions.explanation: Gen. 45:5-7: Joseph told his brothers that God sent him before them to preserve life.

questions.stem: ‘If you will go with me, I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.’ In the statement above, ‘you’ refers to
questions.explanation: Barak said this to Deborah when she told him to lead the army against Sisera (Judges 4:8).

questions.stem: The name Ichabod means
questions.explanation: Phinehas' wife named the child Ichabod, saying 'The glory has departed from Israel' (1 Sam. 4:21).

questions.topic: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
questions.stem: How did David perceive that his child from Bathsheba was dead?
options: Bathsheba lamented the loss of her child.
He saw his servants whispering together.
He received a message to that effect from Joab.
God revealed it to him through Nathan.
questions.explanation: 2 Sam. 12:19: when David saw his servants whispering together, he perceived that the child was dead.

questions.stem: ‘As one falls before the wicked you have fallen.’ This is a part of David’s lamentation over
questions.explanation: David lamented Abner with these words after Joab killed him (2 Sam. 3:33-34).

questions.stem: The mother of the living child asked Solomon to give the child to the other woman because
options: killing the child would serve no useful purpose
her heart yearned for the child
she was confident that the king would ensure justice
she believed the child would recognize her at maturity
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 3:26: her heart yearned for her son, so she pleaded that he be given to the other woman rather than killed.

questions.stem: Hosea’s matrimonial experience symbolizes God’s intention to
options: reform Israel and make her greater
questions.explanation: Hosea bought back his unfaithful wife (Hos. 3), symbolising God's love which redeems unfaithful Israel.

questions.stem: The harlotry of Gomer is compared to Israel’s
questions.explanation: Gomer's harlotry pictures Israel forsaking the LORD for other gods (Hos. 1:2).

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: “Hear the word of the LORD, you rulers of Sodom! Give ear to the teaching of our God, you people of Gomorrah!” The nation referred to as Sodom and Gomorrah in the statement above is
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:1,10: the vision concerned Judah and Jerusalem, whose rulers Isaiah called rulers of Sodom.

questions.stem: Jeremiah was not anxious to accept God’s call to become a prophet because
options: he knew that people would not listen to him
he needed to know God more
he was too young and inexperienced
questions.explanation: Jer. 1:6: 'Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth.'

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: The devil’s principal purpose for tempting Jesus Christ was to
options: show that nobody is above temptation
demonstrate that he controls the world
lure Jesus Christ from his mission
prove that after all, Jesus is only human
questions.explanation: Each temptation sought to divert Jesus from the path of obedient messiahship given by the Father.

questions.stem: ‘Foxes have holes, and birds of the air have nests; but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head.’ The statement above implies that
options: the Son of man needs no house
questions.explanation: Jesus told a would-be follower this to show that following him demands sacrifice (Mt. 8:20; Lk. 9:58).

questions.stem: According to Luke, following Jesus involves
questions.explanation: Lk. 9:23: 'If any man would come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily.'

questions.stem: In the healing ministry of Jesus Christ, which of the following played a very vital role?
questions.explanation: Jesus repeatedly said 'your faith has made you well', and could do few mighty works where there was unbelief.

questions.stem: Jesus healed the only son of the widow of Nain because
options: the widow demonstrated faith in Him
he wanted to make people believe in Him
questions.explanation: Lk. 7:13: when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her.

questions.stem: The healing of the paralytic brought by his four friends demonstrates
options: the power of Jesus to heal all types of diseases
that the friends had faith in the healing power of Jesus
the compassion of Jesus on the sick man
that Jesus has power to forgive sin
questions.explanation: Jesus healed him 'that you may know that the Son of man has authority on earth to forgive sins' (Mk. 2:10).

questions.stem: According to Mark and Luke, the response of blind Bartimaeus to healing was to
options: run to show himself to the priests
speak to the Jews about Jesus
questions.explanation: Mk. 10:52; Lk. 18:43: immediately he received his sight and followed Jesus.

questions.stem: The parable which teaches about God’s judgment is that of the
questions.explanation: In the parable of the weeds the weeds are gathered and burned at the harvest, the close of the age (Mt. 13:40-42).

questions.topic: Parables about love for one another (Lk. 10:25-37; 16:19-31)
questions.stem: The parable of the good Samaritan implies that
options: priests and Levites hardly show love
neighbourliness is expressed in love and concern
a good neighbour must show love to his enemies
questions.explanation: The neighbour was the one who showed mercy (Lk. 10:36-37).

questions.stem: Luke ends the sermon on the plain with an analogy of a building to emphasize the importance of
options: preaching and abiding by the word
questions.explanation: Lk. 6:47-49: he who hears my words and does them is like a man building a house on rock.

questions.stem: Jesus implies in His teaching on adultery, prayer, alms and fasting that these are more of matters of
questions.explanation: In the Sermon on the Mount Jesus stresses inner motive: adultery in the heart, and alms, prayer and fasting done in secret for God.

questions.stem: Jesus’ injunction not to lay up treasure on earth for ourselves implies that the Christian should
questions.explanation: Jesus urged laying up treasure in heaven (Mt. 6:19-20), i.e. being rich toward God through good works.

questions.stem: The seventy disciples who returned from their missionary work were told by Jesus to rejoice because
options: they were well received by people
the spirits were subject to them
their names were written in heaven
questions.explanation: Lk. 10:20: 'do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you; but rejoice that your names are written in heaven.'

questions.stem: According to Matthew, when Jesus was transfigured
options: his face shone like the sun
his body became as white as light
he could only communicate with heaven
questions.explanation: Mt. 17:2: his face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as light.

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: According to Matthew, Jesus entered Jerusalem riding
questions.explanation: Mt. 21:7: the disciples brought the ass and the colt and put their garments on them, and he sat thereon.

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
questions.stem: The prayer of Jesus before his arrest showed that
options: his disciples had not understood him thoroughly
he was not prepared to die on the cross
he wanted his disciples to be prayerful
questions.explanation: In Gethsemane he 'began to be sorrowful and troubled' (Mt. 26:37-38).

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus’ reply to the question above by Pilate was
options: “My kingship is not of this world.”
“Who has made you a prince and a judge over us?”
“Why put me to the test, you hypocrites?”
questions.explanation: Mt. 27:11; Mk. 15:2; Lk. 23:3: Jesus said, 'You have said so.'

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: According to Matthew, when the women went to see the sepulchre, they
options: found that the disciples had been there
saw an angel sitting upon the stone
found the guards rolling back the stone
questions.explanation: Mt. 28:2: an angel of the Lord rolled back the stone and sat upon it.

questions.stem: Jesus used the illustration of the vine to teach that a Christian that abides in Him will surely
questions.explanation: Jn. 15:5: he who abides in me, and I in him, bears much fruit.

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: Two of the seven disciples chosen to serve tables in the early church were
questions.explanation: Acts 6:5 lists Stephen, Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas and Nicolaus.

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: At the Beautiful Gate, Peter and John healed a man who was
questions.explanation: Acts 3:2-8: a man lame from birth was laid at the Beautiful Gate.

questions.stem: The people referred to as pillars of the Jerusalem church, who gave Barnabas and Paul the right hand of fellowship were
questions.explanation: Gal. 2:9: James and Cephas and John, who were reputed to be pillars.

questions.stem: The condition for justification according to Paul is
questions.explanation: Paul teaches that a man is justified by faith in Christ, not by works of the law (Rom. 3:28; Gal. 2:16).

questions.stem: On which of the following grounds will faith be null and promise void?
options: Faith is a necessary condition for justification.
Salvation comes through adherence to the law.
questions.explanation: Rom. 4:14: if it is the adherents of the law who are to be the heirs, faith is null and the promise is void.

questions.stem: According to the Letter of Paul to the Romans, Christians are to yield themselves to God as men who
options: have been raised from death to life
no longer live by the works of law
have listened to the gospel of Christ
questions.explanation: Rom. 6:13: yield yourselves to God as men who have been brought from death to life.

questions.stem: God sent His Son, Jesus Christ, into the world in the likeness of sinful flesh in order
options: that the law might be fulfilled
that man may walk in the flesh
questions.explanation: Rom. 8:3-4: in order that the just requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us.

questions.stem: “... at the name of Jesus every knee should bow ... every tongue confess that Jesus Christ is Lord ...” The statement above demonstrates the Lordship of Jesus over
questions.explanation: Phil. 2:10-11: every knee in heaven, on earth and under the earth shall bow.

questions.stem: Paul told the Corinthians that if any one has caused pain to the church, he should be
questions.explanation: 2 Cor. 2:5-7: you should rather turn to forgive and comfort him.

questions.stem: The greatest spiritual gift to seek for is
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 13:13: the greatest of these is love; 'make love your aim' (1 Cor. 14:1).

questions.stem: One of the civic responsibilities Christians are commanded to carry out is
questions.explanation: Rom. 13:1: let every person be subject to the governing authorities.

questions.stem: In the course of his ministry, Paul worked night and day so that
options: he might not be a burden to any one
he could raise money for the work of the gospel
he could pay the debt he was owing the brethren
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 3:8 (1 Thess. 2:9): we worked night and day, that we might not burden any of you.

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: Those who have fallen asleep before the coming of the Lord are those
questions.explanation: In 1 Thess. 4:13-16 'those who are asleep' are believers who have died; the dead in Christ will rise first.

questions.stem: According to James, the man who prays to God and at the same time doubts is
questions.explanation: James 1:6-8: he who doubts is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.

questions.stem: Peter admonishes Christians that suffering for Christ’s sake brings God’s
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 3:14; 4:14: if you suffer for righteousness' sake / are reproached for the name of Christ, you are blessed.

questions.stem: God made two great lights to
options: rule the day and the night
demarcate between the day and the night
questions.explanation: Gen. 1:16: the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night.

questions.stem: God commanded the earth to bring forth living creatures according to their kinds on the
questions.explanation: Gen. 1:24-31: land creatures and man were made on the sixth day.

questions.stem: When God heard the groaning of the people of Israel in Egypt, He
options: sent a warning to the Pharaoh
questions.explanation: Ex. 2:24: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

questions.stem: “Is it because there are no graves in Egypt that you have taken us away to die in the wilderness?” This question was asked by the Israelites when
options: they were hungry in the wilderness
there was no water for them to drink
the spies brought evil reports about Canaan
questions.explanation: Ex. 14:10-11: when Pharaoh's army drew near at the Red Sea, the people said this to Moses.

questions.stem: God promised to send bread from heaven to the people of Israel, so as to see if they would
questions.explanation: Ex. 16:4: that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law or not.

questions.topic: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
questions.stem: Why did David spare the life of King Saul at Ziph?
options: He did not want to shed blood
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 26:9-11: who can put forth his hand against the LORD's anointed and be guiltless?

questions.topic: David’s repentance and forgiveness (2 Sam. 11; 12:1-15; cf. Ps. 51:1-30)
questions.stem: Nathan told David that although God had put away his sin, he would still be
questions.explanation: 2 Sam. 12:13-14: the LORD has put away your sin... the child that is born to you shall die.

questions.stem: The ark of the covenant brought before Israel and King Solomon contained
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 8:9: there was nothing in the ark except the two tables of stone which Moses put there at Horeb.

questions.stem: Hosea accused Israel of harlotry because
options: the women ran after other husbands
questions.explanation: Hosea uses harlotry as a figure for Israel forsaking the LORD to worship Baal and other gods (Hos. 2; 4:12).

questions.stem: Who among the following was consecrated and appointed prophet before he was born?
questions.explanation: Jer. 1:5: before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.

questions.stem: “Son of man, stand upon your feet, and I will speak with you.” The statement above was made during the call of
questions.explanation: Ezek. 2:1: God addressed Ezekiel as 'son of man' at his call.

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: Satan promised to give Jesus all the kingdoms of the world if He would
options: turn stones to loaves of bread
throw Himself down from the pinnacle of the temple
questions.explanation: Mt. 4:9: all these I will give you, if you will fall down and worship me.

questions.stem: The would-be disciple who wanted to go and bury his father before following Jesus was told that he
options: was not fit for the kingdom of God
should go and proclaim the kingdom of God
should go and build a house first
questions.explanation: Lk. 9:60: leave the dead to bury their own dead; but as for you, go and proclaim the kingdom of God.

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: According to Matthew, the first two disciples to be called by Jesus were
questions.explanation: Mt. 4:18: he saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother.

questions.stem: Jesus had compassion for the five thousand people fed by Him because they were
options: hungry but had no time to eat
strangers from the country and villages far away
poor and had no money to buy food
questions.explanation: Mk. 6:34: he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd.

questions.stem: What was Jesus’ response when the message of Lazarus’ illness reached Him?
options: He asked Mary and Martha to take care of him.
He said that the Son of God may be glorified by it.
He hurried to Bethany to see him.
He instructed that he should be brought to Him.
questions.explanation: Jn. 11:4: this illness is not unto death; it is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified by means of it.

questions.stem: At the country of the Gerasenes, Jesus
options: raised Jairus’ daughter from the dead
raised the widow’s son from the dead
healed the man who had demons
questions.explanation: Mk. 5:1-20; Lk. 8:26-39: Jesus cast the legion of demons out of the man in the country of the Gerasenes.

questions.stem: The parable of the wheat and the tares illustrates that
options: the kingdom of God is already established on earth
both good and evil live in the world
it is impossible to overcome enemies
the wheat cannot grow where there are weeds
questions.explanation: Mt. 13:30, 38: the good seed and the weeds grow together in the world until the harvest.

questions.stem: Jesus’ teaching on swearing is that Christians should
questions.explanation: Mt. 5:34: 'But I say to you, Do not swear at all.'

questions.stem: What blessing has Jesus promised the pure in heart?
options: The earth shall be theirs only
questions.explanation: Mt. 5:8: blessed are the pure in heart, for they shall see God.

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: “... Hosanna to the Son of David! ...” The statement above indicates Jesus’
questions.explanation: 'Son of David' hailed Jesus as the messianic king entering his city (Mt. 21:9).

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: With regard to the triumphal entry, which of the following descriptions is peculiar to Luke?
options: The disciples were sent to bring the animal.
People spread their garments on the road.
The disciples set Jesus on the animal.
questions.explanation: Only Luke says 'they set Jesus upon it' (Lk. 19:35); the others say he sat on it, and Luke does not use 'hosanna'.

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
questions.stem: According to Matthew, when Christ was arrested, He was led to
questions.explanation: Mt. 26:57: those who had seized Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest.

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
questions.stem: The conviction of Jesus by the high priest and the elders was on the ground that He
options: said He would destroy the temple
questions.explanation: Mt. 26:65-66: 'He has uttered blasphemy... He deserves death.'

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: In the account of John about the resurrection, Mary was first asked why she was weeping by
questions.explanation: Jn. 20:12-13: two angels in white said to her, 'Woman, why are you weeping?' before Jesus asked the same.

questions.stem: “Lord, who knowest the hearts of all men, show which one of these two thou hast chosen to take the place ... from which Judas turned aside ...” Who were the two men referred to in the statement above?
questions.explanation: Acts 1:23: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: The criteria for the choice of the seven deacons were
options: good repute and being full of the Spirit
questions.explanation: Acts 6:3: seven men of good repute, full of the Spirit and of wisdom.

questions.stem: At Pentecost, Peter explained that God had promised to pour out His Spirit on all
questions.explanation: Acts 2:17 quoting Joel: I will pour out my Spirit upon all flesh.

questions.stem: The resolution of the Jerusalem council was that the Gentiles should abstain from food offered to idols,
options: unchastity, lying and what is strangled
blood, what is strangled and strong drinks
what is strangled, blood and unchastity
questions.explanation: Acts 15:29: abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from unchastity.

questions.stem: “Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, ... to choose men from among them and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas;” the men chosen were
questions.explanation: Acts 15:22: Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brethren.

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: Peter and John were arrested and imprisoned because they
options: healed a man lame from birth
condemned the Pharisees and the Sadducees
were preaching the gospel of Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 4:1-3: the leaders were annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection, and arrested them.

questions.stem: According to Romans, all who have sinned and fallen short of the glory of God will be justified by
options: the worship of God through Christ
questions.explanation: Rom. 3:23-24: they are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption in Christ Jesus.

questions.stem: According to Paul, what bear witness to the righteousness of God are
questions.explanation: Rom. 3:21: the righteousness of God has been manifested apart from law, although the law and the prophets bear witness to it.

questions.stem: The consequence of setting one’s mind on the things of the flesh is
questions.explanation: Rom. 8:6: to set the mind on the flesh is death.

questions.stem: Paul admonished the Romans to live a new life in Christ by yielding themselves to God as men who
options: have been brought from death to life
will receive judgment in the last days
will meet Christ in God’s kingdom
have suffered for the sake of the gospel
questions.explanation: Rom. 6:13: yield yourselves to God as men who have been brought from death to life.

questions.stem: “But now that faith has come, we are no longer under a custodian; ...” Custodian here means the
questions.explanation: Gal. 3:24-25: the law was our custodian until Christ came.

questions.stem: Paul, writing to the Philippians, said that God highly exalted Christ and bestowed on Him the name which is above every name because He was
questions.explanation: Phil. 2:8-9: he humbled himself and became obedient unto death; therefore God has highly exalted him.

questions.stem: According to Paul, Christians should forgive one another so that
options: Satan may not gain advantage over them
they may not perish in sin
questions.explanation: 2 Cor. 2:10-11: to keep Satan from gaining the advantage over us.

questions.stem: Spiritual gifts, according to Paul, should be used for the
options: upliftment of individuals in the church
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 14:12: strive to excel in building up (edifying) the church.

questions.stem: Paul considered the Philippians’ gifts to him as
options: an exhibition of Christian maturity and generosity
a fragrant offering and a sacrifice acceptable to God
questions.explanation: Phil. 4:18: the gifts you sent, a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God.

questions.stem: ‘For rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad.’ Christians, therefore, must do what is good and they would
options: be left alone to preach the Gospel
questions.explanation: Rom. 13:3: then do what is good, and you will receive his approval.

questions.stem: ‘Now we command you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you keep away from any brother who is living in idleness ...’ The statement above was made to teach
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 3:6-12: Paul commands that idle people work quietly and earn their own living.

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: The second coming of Jesus Christ, according to Paul, will be preceded by the coming of
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 2:3: that day will not come unless the rebellion comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed.

questions.stem: ‘Is it not the rich who oppress you, is it not they who drag you into court?’ James asked this question in his teaching on
questions.explanation: James 2:1-7 rebukes partiality shown to the rich against the poor.

questions.stem: The wisdom of God is necessary for salvation, hence James teaches that Christians should
options: ask for it when they can
endure all trials to get it
ask in faith to get it
questions.explanation: James 1:5-6: if any lacks wisdom, let him ask God... but let him ask in faith, with no doubting.

questions.topic: Interpersonal relationships among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb. 13:1-21)
questions.stem: The importance of love in the teaching of Peter is that it
options: brings together all believers in the community
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 4:8: hold unfailing your love for one another, since love covers a multitude of sins.

questions.topic: Interpersonal relationships among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb. 13:1-21)
questions.stem: According to Peter, when the Chief Shepherd is manifested, Christians will
options: cast all their anxieties on Him
obtain the unfading crown of glory
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 5:4: when the chief Shepherd is manifested you will obtain the unfading crown of glory.

questions.stem: “Behold, I have given you every plant yielding seed which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed in its fruit; ...” In the statement above, God made all provision for man to
questions.explanation: Gen. 1:29: 'you shall have them for food.'

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: God told Noah that ‘Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed; ...’ because
options: man is made in God’s image
blood is the life of man
questions.explanation: Gen. 9:6: for God made man in his own image.

questions.stem: What did God promise the Israelites after their rescue from Babylon to make them fear Him for ever?
options: A new heart and a new life
A new covenant and a new spirit
questions.explanation: Jer. 32:37-39: I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me for ever.

questions.stem: The Lord appeared to Abraham and promised his descendants the land of the Canaanites at
questions.explanation: Gen. 12:6-7: at the oak of Moreh the LORD appeared and said, 'To your descendants I will give this land.'

questions.stem: When Joseph narrated his second dream, he was rebuked by Jacob because the dream would
options: make his brothers all the more jealous
subject his parents to his authority
send the family to Egypt as slaves
