questions.stem: King Saul asked Jesse to send David to him because he wanted David to
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 16:19-22: Saul sent for David to play the lyre and asked Jesse, "Let David remain in my service".

questions.stem: The new covenant God made with the house of Israel and the house of Judah was written on
questions.explanation: Jer. 31:33: "I will put my law within them, and I will write it upon their hearts."

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: "All the words which the LORD has spoken we will do." What was Moses' response to this declaration by the Israelites?
options: He asked them to pick twelve stones to represent the tribes
He offered peace offerings to the LORD
He charged them to walk faithfully before the LORD
He said that the LORD was witness to their declaration
questions.explanation: Ex. 24:3-5: after the people's declaration Moses built an altar with twelve pillars and had burnt offerings and peace offerings sacrificed to the LORD.

questions.topic: The flood and God’s covenant with Noah (Gen. 6:1-22; 7:1-24; 9:1-17)
questions.stem: The sign of the covenant between God and Noah for all future generations was
questions.explanation: Gen. 9:12-13: "I set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be a sign of the covenant."

questions.stem: The signs that God showed to Moses at his call were meant to
options: convince the people that he had been sent by God
portray him as superior to the Egyptian magicians
enable him to perform miracles before Pharaoh
convince Pharaoh that he was the prophet of God
questions.explanation: Ex. 4:1-5: the signs were given "that they may believe that the LORD... has appeared to you".

questions.stem: King Josiah defiled Topheth, which was in the valley of the sons of Hinnom, during his reform so that
options: he might revive the worship of the sun god
he might pull down Topheth and break Molech into pieces
no one might sacrifice human beings again to Molech
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:10: he defiled Topheth "that no one might burn his son or his daughter as an offering to Molech".

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: Amos declared that the Jews who built houses of hewn stone would not dwell in them because they
questions.explanation: Amos 5:11: "because you trample upon the poor... you have built houses of hewn stone, but you shall not dwell in them".

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: What acts of righteousness did Isaiah admonish his people to demonstrate?
options: Helping the poor and offering sacrifice
Defending the orphans and respecting the widows
Avoiding evils and praying for others
Learning to do good and seeking justice
questions.explanation: Isa. 1:17: "learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; defend the fatherless, plead for the widow."

questions.stem: God promised the faithless Israelites that if they repented of their sins and returned to Him, He would
options: deliver their enemies into their hands
give them favour in the sight of the nations
give them shepherds after his own heart
questions.explanation: Jer. 3:14-15: "Return, O faithless children... And I will give you shepherds after my own heart."

questions.stem: "...When my soul fainted within me, I remembered the LORD; and my prayer came to thee..." The prayer above was offered by Jonah
options: in the belly of the fish
questions.explanation: Jonah 2:1-7: Jonah prayed this prayer from the belly of the fish.

questions.stem: "The ark of the God of Israel must not remain with us..." The Philistines who made the statement above were anxious to get rid of the ark because
options: the hand of God was heavy upon them
the Israelites had mustered forces against them
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 5:7: "...for his hand is heavy upon us and upon Dagon our god."

questions.stem: "At that time shall arise... the great prince who has charge of your people..." In the statement above by Daniel, the great prince refers to
questions.explanation: Dan. 12:1: "At that time shall arise Michael, the great prince who has charge of your people."

questions.stem: According to Hosea, the LORD would not have pity upon the children of his faithless wife because
options: their mother had not shown pity on them
their mother had played the harlot
questions.explanation: Hos. 2:4-5: "Upon her children also I will have no pity... For their mother has played the harlot."

questions.stem: God decided not to bring evil in Ahab's days but in the days of his son because Ahab
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:29: "Because he has humbled himself before me, I will not bring the evil in his days."

questions.stem: When the Babylonians captured King Zedekiah, they
options: assaulted his wives in his presence
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:7: they slew his sons before his eyes, then put out the eyes of Zedekiah and took him to Babylon.

questions.topic: Obedience and Rewards: Abraham (Gen. 22:1-19), the three Hebrew youths (Dan. 3:1-30), David (1 Sam. 30:1-20)
questions.stem: The men who threw Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego into the fire were
options: amazed that the Hebrews were not burnt
assisted to escape from being burnt
questions.explanation: Dan. 3:22: the flame of the fire slew the men who took up Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego.

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: "Hear this word, you cows of Bashan... who oppress the poor, who crush the needy..." Cows of Bashan in the statement above refers to the
questions.explanation: Amos 4:1 addresses the "cows of Bashan, who are in the mountain of Samaria" - the luxurious women of Samaria who say to their husbands, "Bring, that we may drink".

questions.stem: "It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am no better than my fathers." The prayer above was said by Elijah when he
options: had no water to drink at the brook Cherith
learnt that Ahab was looking for him
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 19:1-4: after Jezebel threatened his life, Elijah fled to the wilderness and prayed that he might die.

questions.topic: Response to the state of Judah (Neh. 2; 4:1-23; Ezra 3:4; 5; 6; 7)
questions.stem: In his effort to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, Nehemiah prayed against the insults of
questions.explanation: Neh. 4:1-5: Nehemiah prayed, "Hear, O our God, for we are despised", against the taunts of Sanballat and Tobiah.

questions.stem: According to Luke, Jesus healed the epileptic boy by
options: telling the boy to have faith
binding the evil spirit in him
questions.explanation: Luke 9:42: "Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy."

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: According to Luke, Jesus' last words on the cross were
options: "Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit"
"Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do"
questions.explanation: Luke 23:46: "Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit!" And having said this he breathed his last.

questions.topic: Parables about love for one another (Lk. 10:25-37; 16:19-31)
questions.stem: "Father Abraham, have mercy upon me, and send Lazarus..." Abraham could not grant the rich man's request because
options: the rich man lived in luxury while on earth
there was a chasm between them
he had no pity on the rich man
his dogs used to lick Lazarus's sores
questions.explanation: Luke 16:26: "between us and you a great chasm has been fixed" so none may cross.

questions.stem: In the story of the transfiguration of Jesus, Moses and Elijah represented the
questions.explanation: Moses stands for the Law and Elijah for the Prophets, both bearing witness to Jesus.

questions.topic: The Door, the Lamb and the Good Shepherd (Jn. 1:29-34; 10:1-18)
questions.stem: "...but he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep..." The door in the statement refers to
questions.explanation: John 10:7-9: "I am the door of the sheep... if any one enters by me, he will be saved."

questions.stem: In order to fulfil the law of Moses, Jesus told the leper He had healed to go and
questions.explanation: Luke 5:14 / Mt. 8:4: "go and show yourself to the priest" as Moses commanded.

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: The Jewish religious leaders arrested and imprisoned the apostles the second time because
options: they performed miracles in the name of Jesus
the high priest and the Sadducees accused them of treason
the high priest and the Sadducees were jealous
questions.explanation: Acts 5:17-18: the high priest and the Sadducees, "filled with jealousy", arrested the apostles and put them in the common prison.

questions.stem: After the mission of the seventy, Jesus declared that he had given them
options: authority over all the power of the enemy
the gift of knowledge of the word
questions.explanation: Luke 10:19: "I have given you authority... over all the power of the enemy."

questions.stem: Jesus did not go immediately to attend to Lazarus, who was reported sick, because he
options: wanted His disciples to believe in Him
was too busy attending to other people
did not know how serious the sickness was
questions.explanation: John 11:15: "for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe."

questions.stem: In the parable of the wheat and tares, the harvest time refers to the
questions.explanation: Mt. 13:39: "the harvest is the close of the age, and the reapers are angels."

questions.topic: Christians living among non-Christians (1 Pet. 2:3-25; Rom. 15:1-2)
questions.stem: Peter teaches that good Christian conduct is characterized by love and
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 2:17 (cf. 1:17): "Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honour the emperor"; believers are to conduct themselves with fear.

questions.stem: Paul teaches that the exercise of spiritual gifts by individual believers should be used to promote
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 12:7, 12-26: gifts are given "for the common good" so that the members of the one body work together and care for one another.

questions.topic: Interpersonal relationships among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb. 13:1-21)
questions.stem: Peter advises the elders to tend the flock of God with
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 5:2: tend the flock "not by constraint but willingly... not for shameful gain but eagerly".

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: Paul warned the Thessalonians against the deceit of false teachers concerning
options: activities of the man of sin
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 2:1-3: "concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ... Let no one deceive you" that the day of the Lord has come.

questions.stem: Paul described the gifts he received from the Philippians as
questions.explanation: Phil. 4:18: "a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God."

questions.stem: According to Paul, the purpose of the law is
options: to increase the knowledge of sin
to bring about justification by faith
to promote faith in the crucified Christ
questions.explanation: Rom. 3:20: "through the law comes knowledge of sin" (cf. Rom. 7:7).

questions.stem: The man who stirred up the people against Paul in Ephesus was
questions.explanation: Acts 19:24-29: Demetrius the silversmith gathered the craftsmen and the city was filled with confusion.

questions.stem: Paul teaches that believers have been buried and raised with Christ so that they might
options: grow in the knowledge of Christ
questions.explanation: Rom. 6:4: "buried therefore with him by baptism... so that... we too might walk in newness of life."

questions.stem: According to James, because believers hold the faith of the Lord Jesus Christ, they should
questions.explanation: James 2:1: "show no partiality as you hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ."

questions.topic: The signs of the Coming of Christ (1 Thess. 4:13-18; 2 Thess. 2:1-12)
questions.stem: According to Paul, God would send a strong delusion upon those who will perish because they
options: did not show love to the brethren
questions.explanation: 2 Thess. 2:10-12: because they refused to love the truth, God sends upon them a strong delusion, that all may be condemned who did not believe the truth.

questions.stem: According to Romans, justification is by faith through
options: being filled with the Holy Spirit
questions.explanation: Rom. 3:24: believers "are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus".

questions.topic: Preparation for His coming (1 Thess. 5:1-11; 2 Pet. 3:1-13; Matt. 25:31-46)
questions.stem: Peter teaches that Christians should prepare for the day of the Lord by
questions.explanation: 2 Pet. 3:11-12: "what sort of persons ought you to be in lives of holiness and godliness, waiting for... the day of God".

questions.topic: David’s submission to the will of God (1 Sam. 26:1-25; 2 Sam. 12:15-25)
questions.stem: David did not allow Abishai to destroy Saul because he
options: believed in the judgement of God
wanted to avoid being guilty before the LORD
wanted to disarm Saul before killing him
wanted to see if Saul would repent eventually
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 26:9: "who can put forth his hand against the LORD's anointed, and be guiltless?"

questions.stem: The reward for total obedience to the commandments of God is
questions.explanation: Deut. 30:16-20: loving and obeying the LORD "means life to you and length of days".

questions.stem: Adam named his wife Eve because she was
questions.explanation: Gen. 3:20: "The man called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living."

questions.stem: What was the immediate reaction of Moses when he cast his rod on the ground at Mount Horeb and it became a serpent?
options: He took it by the tail
questions.explanation: Ex. 4:3: the rod became a serpent "and Moses fled from it"; only afterwards did he take it by the tail.

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: The consequence of King Solomon's failure to keep the LORD's commandment was
options: God's promise to tear away part of the kingdom
the rebellion of the vassal states against his rule
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 11:11-13: "I will surely tear the kingdom from you" - all but one tribe, from his son's hand.

questions.stem: According to Prophet Isaiah, the creative ability of God is likened to that of a
questions.explanation: Isa. 64:8 (cf. 45:9): "we are the clay, and thou art our potter; we are all the work of thy hand."

questions.stem: "David departed from there and escaped... and when his brothers and all his father's house heard it..." In the statement above, where did David escape to?
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 22:1: "David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam."

questions.stem: Hiram, King of Tyre, was friendly with King Solomon because he
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 5:1: "Hiram always loved David", so he sent servants to Solomon.

questions.stem: "Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you..." Where was Abraham when this command was given?
questions.explanation: Gen. 11:31-12:4: Terah's family had settled in Haran, and Abram departed from Haran at seventy-five in obedience to this call.

questions.stem: The LORD repented of the evil which he intended for His people because Moses
options: burnt the golden calf which the people made
broke the tablets out of his hands
made the people drink of the water of the burnt calf
reminded Him of his promise to Abraham, Isaac and Israel
questions.explanation: Ex. 32:13-14: Moses said, "Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel", and the LORD repented of the evil.

questions.stem: The altar that Gideon built at the oak of Ophrah was called
questions.explanation: Judg. 6:24: Gideon built an altar there "and called it, The LORD is peace".

questions.stem: The second creation story ends with the institution of
questions.explanation: Gen. 2:24: "a man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife" - the account ends with marriage.

questions.topic: A Man After God’s Own Heart
questions.stem: The greatest domestic problem King David experienced which almost cost him his kingdom was
options: the proclamation of Adonijah as king
the revolt of Absalom against him
questions.explanation: 2 Sam. 15-18: Absalom's revolt drove David out of Jerusalem and nearly took his throne.

questions.stem: The declaration by God that he would make a nation of the son of the slave woman meant that He
options: was not partial towards Isaac and Ishmael
did not like the way Ishmael was sent out by Abraham
was responsible for sending Ishmael out of Abraham's house
questions.explanation: Gen. 21:13: "I will make a nation of the son of the slave woman also, because he is your offspring."

questions.stem: "...The earth produces of itself, first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear..." The statement above was made by Jesus in the parable of the
questions.explanation: Mark 4:26-29: the parable of the seed growing secretly.

questions.stem: Peter became frightened as he walked on the sea because
questions.explanation: Mt. 14:30: "when he saw the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out".

questions.stem: What did the blind man by the roadside near Jericho do on receiving his sight?
options: He jumped for joy and went away
He thanked Jesus for healing him
He gave praise to God for making him whole
questions.explanation: Luke 18:43: "immediately he received his sight and followed him, glorifying God".

questions.topic: Crucifixion and burial of Jesus (Mt. 27:32-66; Lk. 23:26-56; Mk. 15:16-47; Jn. 19:17-42)
questions.stem: The order of the crucifixion events according to Luke's Gospel is
options: crucifixion, lots casting for His dress, scoffing and mockery
mockery, lots casting for His dress, scoffing and crucifixion
lots casting for His dress, mockery, scoffing and crucifixion
crucifixion, scoffing, mockery and lots casting for His dress
questions.explanation: Luke 23:33-36: they crucified him, cast lots to divide his garments, the rulers scoffed, and the soldiers mocked him.

questions.stem: The angel told Zechariah that John the Baptist would drink no wine nor strong drink because he would
options: only eat locusts and wild honey
be filled with the Holy Spirit
baptize sinners who would come to him
questions.explanation: Luke 1:15: "he shall drink no wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit".

questions.stem: The condition Peter gave for a person that would replace Judas Iscariot was that he must be
options: a disciple of John the Baptist
questions.explanation: Acts 1:21-22: one who accompanied them all the time the Lord Jesus went in and out among them, to become a witness to his resurrection.

questions.stem: "They have no wine." Jesus' immediate response to the statement above was
options: "...Draw some out and take it to the steward of the feast"
"O woman, what have you to do with me? My hour has not yet come"
questions.explanation: John 2:3-4: to his mother's remark Jesus replied, "O woman, what have you to do with me? My hour has not yet come."

questions.stem: The Macedonians who travelled with Paul to Ephesus were
questions.explanation: Acts 19:29: the mob dragged "Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul's companions in travel".

questions.stem: According to the first Epistle of John, to have the Son is to have
questions.explanation: 1 John 5:12: "He who has the Son has life."

questions.stem: In the explanation of the parable of the weeds, Jesus said that the righteous will
options: live forever in the kingdom of God
be set aside from all causes of sin
enter into glory with the Son of man
shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom
questions.explanation: Mt. 13:43: "Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father."

questions.stem: The resolution of the Council at Jerusalem was that the Gentiles should abstain from
options: adultery, greed, strangled meat and divination
homosexuality, idolatry, fornication and strangled meat
idolatry, unchastity, strangled meat and blood
questions.explanation: Acts 15:20, 29: abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols, from blood, from what is strangled and from unchastity.

questions.topic: Parable about wealth: the rich fool (Lk. 12:13-21)
questions.stem: "...And I will say to my soul, Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, be merry..." God's response to the statement above was that
options: the servant should enter into the rest of his Lord
his soul was required of him
his soul should be satisfied with his increase
he should lay up more treasures for himself
questions.explanation: Luke 12:20: "Fool! This night your soul is required of you."

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before the High Priest (Mt. 26:36-75; Mk. 14:53-72; Lk. 22:66-71)
questions.stem: Before the cock crowed, Peter denied Jesus three times. Who was the first person to recognize him as one of the disciples?
questions.explanation: Luke 22:56: "a maid, seeing him as he sat in the light... said, This man also was with him."

questions.stem: The woman with the flow of blood touched the garment of Jesus because
options: she had heard the reports about Jesus
she had suffered much under many physicians
the crowd could not allow her to speak to Jesus
she believed that she would be well
questions.explanation: Mark 5:28: "For she said, If I touch even his garments, I shall be made well."

questions.topic: Preparation for His coming (1 Thess. 5:1-11; 2 Pet. 3:1-13; Matt. 25:31-46)
questions.stem: In Paul's letter to the Thessalonians, believers were admonished to prepare for the Second Coming of Christ by
questions.explanation: 1 Thess. 5:6: "So then let us not sleep, as others do, but let us keep awake and be sober."

questions.stem: Paul taught the Romans that while they were yet enemies of God, they were reconciled to him by the
questions.explanation: Rom. 5:10: "while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son".

questions.stem: Paul declared to the believers in Corinth that no one can say "Jesus is Lord" except by
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 12:3: "no one can say Jesus is Lord except by the Holy Spirit."

questions.stem: In Colossians, Paul admonished believers not to lie to one another because they
options: were joint heirs with Christ in the kingdom
were waiting for the Second Coming of Christ
had put off the old nature with its practices
had known the truth from the very beginning
questions.explanation: Col. 3:9: "Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old nature with its practices."

questions.stem: Paul teaches that believers who maintain good conduct before governing authorities shall
questions.explanation: Rom. 13:3: "Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval."

questions.topic: Interpersonal relationships among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb. 13:1-21)
questions.stem: According to Peter, when the chief Shepherd is manifested, the elders would obtain the
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 5:4: "when the chief Shepherd is manifested you will obtain the unfading crown of glory."

questions.stem: Paul boasted about the believers in Corinth for their
questions.explanation: 2 Cor. 9:1-2: concerning the offering for the saints, "I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the people of Macedonia".

questions.stem: God exalted the name of Jesus above every other name in heaven and on earth because
options: Jesus was born in the likeness of man
as Son of God, He counted equality with God a thing to be grasped
in humility, He counted others better than Himself
He humbled himself to be born in human form and was obedient unto death
questions.explanation: Phil. 2:7-9: he humbled himself and became obedient unto death, "Therefore God has highly exalted him".

questions.stem: How did Joshua react to the defeat of the Israelites by the men of Ai?
questions.explanation: Josh. 7:6: "Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark."

questions.stem: Hosea declares that the upright walk in the ways of the LORD, but transgressors
questions.explanation: Hos. 14:9: "the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them."

questions.stem: After Nebuchadnezzar had destroyed Jerusalem, he took the inhabitants into exile but left behind the
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:14; 25:12: none remained "except the poorest people of the land" to be vinedressers and ploughmen.

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: According to Amos, the type of famine God said he would send upon the people of Israel was
options: not hearing the word of the LORD
hunger for baskets of summer fruits
questions.explanation: Amos 8:11: "not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD."

questions.stem: "...The soul that sins shall die." The statement above by Prophet Ezekiel means that
options: a sinner shall not escape punishment
the wages of sin is death
God will judge the soul of a sinner
every person is responsible for his own sin
questions.explanation: Ezek. 18:4, 20: the son shall not suffer for the father's iniquity - each person bears responsibility for his own sin.

questions.stem: The consequence of Hiel's building of Jericho was that he
options: was made a commander in Ahab's army
was highly respected by his tribe
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 16:34: he laid its foundation at the cost of Abiram his first-born and set up its gates at the cost of Segub, fulfilling Joshua's curse.

questions.stem: "...I send you to the people of Israel, to a nation of rebels." The statement above was God's message to
questions.explanation: Ezek. 2:3: "Son of man, I send you to the people of Israel, to a nation of rebels."

questions.stem: Daniel was set up to be thrown to the lions by the
options: lords and nobles of the Medes
questions.explanation: Dan. 6:4-7: the presidents and satraps plotted against Daniel and got the king to sign the interdict.

questions.stem: According to Hosea, one of the punishments for the sins of Israel was that
options: they would not receive divine revelation
they would eat but would not be satisfied
the LORD would send famine upon the land
questions.explanation: Hos. 4:10: "They shall eat, but not be satisfied; they shall play the harlot, but not multiply."

questions.stem: Elisha knew of the covetous act of Gehazi because
options: he went with him in spirit
he saw the gifts with him
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 5:26: "Did I not go with you in spirit when the man turned from his chariot to meet you?" (The paper prints "Elijah"; the prophet was Elisha.)

questions.stem: Moses sent men to spy out the land of Canaan in order to
options: know if it was good or bad
know if it was flowing with milk and honey
questions.explanation: Num. 13:18-19: "see what the land is... and whether the land that they dwell in is good or bad".

questions.stem: The two sons of Samuel that became judges in Israel were
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 8:1-2: "The name of his first-born son was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah."

questions.stem: When the glory of the LORD appeared to Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Zin, the LORD said they should
options: tell the rock before their eyes to yield its water
strike the rock with the rod to bring out water for them
fetch water for the people and their cattle
tell the people to go around the rock
questions.explanation: Num. 20:8: "tell the rock before their eyes to yield its water".

questions.stem: The last event that boosted Gideon's courage to go against the Midianites was the
options: appearance of the angel who called him a man of valour
sign in which God caused the dew to be on the fleece
test God gave Gideon's men at the waterside
dream told by the Midianites about the barley bread
questions.explanation: Judg. 7:13-15: hearing the Midianite's dream of the barley loaf, Gideon worshipped and roused Israel to attack.

questions.stem: Saul visited the witch of Endor when he was besieged by the
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 28:4-7: the Philistines encamped at Shunem; Saul was afraid and sought a medium.

questions.stem: Why did Saul tell the Kenites to go away from among the Amalekites?
options: God did not tell him to destroy the Kenites
The Kenites showed kindness to Israel
The Kenites had a blood covenant with Israel
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 15:6: "for you showed kindness to all the people of Israel when they came up out of Egypt".

questions.stem: "...And they shall be my people, and I will be their God..." This covenant was made with Israel through Prophet
questions.explanation: Jer. 31:33 (cf. 32:38): the new covenant through Jeremiah - "I will be their God, and they shall be my people".

questions.stem: Joseph was made prime minister in Egypt because he
options: interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's servants in the prison
resisted the temptation by Potiphar's wife
was a faithful and upright man
interpreted Pharaoh's dream and counselled him on what to do
questions.explanation: Gen. 41:33-41: after interpreting the dream and advising Pharaoh to appoint a wise man over Egypt, Joseph was set over the land.

questions.stem: Nehemiah in exile functioned as the King's
questions.explanation: Neh. 1:11: "Now I was cupbearer to the king."

questions.stem: In the days of Uzziah, Isaiah saw a vision concerning
questions.explanation: Isa. 1:1: "The vision of Isaiah... which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah..."

questions.stem: God said that any member of Ahab's family who died in the open country would be
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:24: "any one belonging to Ahab who dies in the open country the birds of the air shall eat."

questions.stem: "Take away all iniquity; accept that which is good..." What was the iniquity Hosea was referring to in the statement above?
questions.explanation: Hos. 14:2-8: Israel is to say "We will say no more, Our God, to the work of our hands"; Ephraim has nothing more to do with idols.

questions.stem: According to Jeremiah, the role of the shepherds which God will give to His people is to
options: feed the people with knowledge and understanding
heal the guilt of the people
gather the scattered children of Israel
questions.explanation: Jer. 3:15: "shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding."

questions.topic: Obedience and Rewards: Abraham (Gen. 22:1-19), the three Hebrew youths (Dan. 3:1-30), David (1 Sam. 30:1-20)
questions.stem: King Nebuchadnezzar assembled the satraps, the prefects and the governors for
questions.explanation: Dan. 3:2: he sent to assemble the satraps, prefects and governors "to come to the dedication of the image".

questions.stem: Where did Elijah kill all the prophets of Baal after the contest with Ahab?
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 18:40: "Elijah brought them down to the brook Kishon, and killed them there."

questions.stem: "...The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge..." This proverb means that
options: parents are punished for the sins of their children
children are punished for the sins of their parents
parents are punished for the sins of their grandparents
great grandchildren are punished for the sins of their forefathers
questions.explanation: Ezek. 18:2 (Jer. 31:29): the proverb claimed the children suffer for what their fathers did; God rejects it.

questions.stem: After Jonah had been thrown into the sea and the sea ceased from its raging, the men with him
options: praised the LORD for saving them
feared the LORD, offered sacrifice and made vows
rowed hard to bring the ship back to land
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:16: "the men feared the LORD exceedingly, and they offered a sacrifice to the LORD and made vows."

questions.stem: Zedekiah, the king of Judah, was captured by the army of the Chaldeans
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 25:5: "the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and overtook him in the plains of Jericho"; he was then brought to Riblah.

questions.topic: The mission of the twelve (Mt. 10:5-15; Mk. 6:7-13; Lk. 9:1-16)
questions.stem: According to Luke, the mandate given to the twelve at their commissioning was to
options: rid the entire region of Galilee of evil spirits
preach the gospel to the poor
preach the kingdom of God and heal
go about doing good to all people
questions.explanation: Luke 9:2: "he sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal."

questions.topic: The trial of Jesus before Pilate (Mt. 27:11-26; Mk. 15:1-15; Lk. 23:1-5, 13-25; Jn. 18:28-40; 19:1-16)
questions.stem: According to John, the accusation the Jews levelled against Jesus before Pilate was that He was
questions.explanation: John 18:30: "If this man were not an evildoer, we would not have handed him over."

questions.topic: The call of the first disciples (Mt. 4:18-22; 9:9-13; Mk. 1:16-20; 2:13-17; Lk. 5:1-11, 27-32)
questions.stem: "...Go and learn what this means, 'I desire mercy, and not sacrifice'..." Jesus made this statement in connection with the
questions.explanation: Mt. 9:10-13: when the Pharisees objected to his eating with tax collectors and sinners at Matthew's house.

questions.stem: Jesus did not go with the centurion to heal his servant because the centurion
options: spoke to Jesus as a man under authority
said he was not worthy for Jesus to come under his roof
questions.explanation: Luke 7:6-7 / Mt. 8:8: "I am not worthy to have you come under my roof; but say the word."

questions.stem: The condition Jesus required from Jairus in order to heal his daughter was that he should
options: put out those weeping in the house
questions.explanation: Mark 5:36: "Do not fear, only believe."

questions.stem: According to Peter's speech on the day of Pentecost, God made Jesus
questions.explanation: Acts 2:36: "God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified."

questions.stem: "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved." The men who taught the above came from
questions.explanation: Acts 15:1: "some men came down from Judea" teaching this at Antioch.

questions.topic: The Bread of Life and the Living Water (Jn. 4:7-15; 6:25-58)
questions.stem: According to John, Jesus said the work of God is
options: feeding the hungry who are in need
believing in Him whom He has sent
questions.explanation: John 6:29: "This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent."

questions.stem: Why was Paul arrested and detained at Philippi?
options: He never stopped proclaiming Jesus as Lord and Saviour
The Jews did not want him to preach in the Gentiles' territories
He cast out the spirit of soothsaying from a slave girl
He was preaching the unknown God
questions.explanation: Acts 16:16-23: after Paul exorcised the slave girl, her owners dragged Paul and Silas to the magistrates.

questions.stem: Jesus said His disciples had been made clean by
options: the word He spoke to them
questions.explanation: John 15:3: "You are already made clean by the word which I have spoken to you."

questions.stem: Following the death of Stephen, the only group of believers not scattered by the great persecution against the Jerusalem church were the
questions.explanation: Acts 8:1: "they were all scattered... except the apostles."

questions.stem: The first and second in the order of hierarchy of spiritual gifts enumerated by Paul are
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 12:28: "first apostles, second prophets, third teachers..."

questions.stem: According to Galatians, Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by
questions.explanation: Gal. 3:13: "Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, having become a curse for us."

questions.stem: According to Paul, a ruler does not bear the sword in vain but he
options: leads men into the ways of God
executes God's wrath on the wrongdoer
rules as influenced by the people
questions.explanation: Rom. 13:4: "he is the servant of God to execute his wrath on the wrongdoer."

questions.topic: Christians as Joint Heirs with Christ
questions.stem: In Paul's Epistle to the Galatians, as long as an heir is a child, he is under
questions.explanation: Gal. 4:1-2: the heir, while a child, "is under guardians and trustees until the date set by the father".

questions.stem: According to Peter, believers who are reproached for the name of Christ are blessed because the spirit of
options: glory and of God rests upon them
love and God rests upon them
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 4:14: "the spirit of glory and of God rests upon you."

questions.topic: Interpersonal relationships among Christians (1 Pet. 5:1-4; Rom. 12:3-21; 2 Pet. 1:3-11; Heb. 13:1-21)
questions.stem: In interpersonal relationships, Paul advises believers to
questions.explanation: Rom. 12:3: "not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think, but to think with sober judgment."

questions.stem: In his letter to Philemon, Paul described Onesimus as his
questions.explanation: Philem. 10: "I appeal to you for my child, Onesimus, whose father I have become in my imprisonment."

questions.topic: Preparation for His coming (1 Thess. 5:1-11; 2 Pet. 3:1-13; Matt. 25:31-46)
questions.stem: In Thessalonians, Paul advises believers awaiting the coming of the Lord to put on the
questions.explanation: 1 Thess. 5:8: "put on the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet the hope of salvation."

questions.stem: According to Corinthians, the same Spirit gives varieties of gifts while the same Lord gives varieties of
questions.explanation: 1 Cor. 12:4-5: "varieties of gifts, but the same Spirit; and there are varieties of service, but the same Lord."

questions.topic: Problems of communal living and solutions (Acts 5:1-11; 6:1-6)
questions.stem: What effect did the sudden death of Ananias and Sapphira have on the early disciples?
options: Many more disciples were won to God
questions.explanation: Acts 5:11: "great fear came upon the whole church, and upon all who heard of these things."

questions.topic: The commissioning and mission of Paul (Acts 13; 14:1-20)
questions.stem: Paul and Barnabas were sent out on the first missionary work from Antioch to Seleucia by the
questions.explanation: Acts 13:4: "So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia."

questions.stem: "...We must work the works of him who sent me, while it is day; night comes, when no one can work." Jesus made the statement above at the healing of the
questions.explanation: John 9:1-7: spoken before healing the man born blind.

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: "They have taken the Lord out of the tomb, and we do not know where they have laid him." What happened immediately after Mary Magdalene made the statement above?
options: Peter and the other disciple went towards the tomb
The guards were afraid and ran away from the tomb
Mary stood weeping outside the tomb
Two angels appeared to Mary by the tomb
questions.explanation: John 20:2-3: "Peter then came out with the other disciple, and they went toward the tomb."

questions.topic: The arrest and imprisonment of Peter and John (Acts 3; 4:1-22; 5:17-42; 12:1-24)
questions.stem: "...For if this plan or this undertaking is of men, it will fail; but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them..." "Them" in Gamaliel's statement above refers to
questions.explanation: Acts 5:29-39: Gamaliel advised the council concerning Peter and the apostles.

questions.stem: Jesus declared that men love darkness rather than light because
questions.explanation: John 3:19: "men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil."

questions.stem: "...This Jesus God raised up, and of that we all are witnesses..." The statement above was made by Peter on the occasion of his
options: sermon on the day of Pentecost
release from prison by the Jews
healing of the lame man at the gate called Beautiful
address to the disciples for the replacement of Judas
questions.explanation: Acts 2:32: from Peter's sermon on the day of Pentecost.

questions.stem: According to John, he who does not believe in the only Son of God is
questions.explanation: John 3:18: "he who does not believe is condemned already."

questions.topic: Resurrection, Appearances and Ascension of Jesus
questions.stem: "...Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know the things that have happened there in these days?" The things being referred to in the statement above are the
options: arrest, trials and judgment of Jesus
crucifixion, death and resurrection of Jesus
triumphal entry and cleansing of the temple
questions.explanation: Luke 24:18-24: Cleopas tells of Jesus' condemnation and crucifixion and the report that he is alive.

questions.stem: According to Paul, just as the law came to increase trespass, so sin came to increase
questions.explanation: Rom. 5:20: "Law came in, to increase the trespass; but where sin increased, grace abounded all the more."

questions.stem: Paul declares that Christians do not all have the same function, but they have gifts that differ according to
questions.explanation: Rom. 12:4-6: "Having gifts that differ according to the grace given to us..."

questions.stem: According to Romans, as one man's trespass led to condemnation for all, so one man's act of righteousness leads to
options: acquittal and life for all men
salvation and new life for all men
justification and hope for all men
sanctification and life for all men
questions.explanation: Rom. 5:18: "one man's act of righteousness leads to acquittal and life for all men."

questions.stem: "And let steadfastness have its full effect..." What does James say would be the outcome of this effect?
questions.explanation: James 1:4: "that you may be perfect and complete, lacking in nothing."

questions.stem: "Have this mind among yourselves, which you have in Christ Jesus..." This mind in Paul's statement above means a mind of
questions.explanation: Phil. 2:3-8: the mind of Christ, who humbled himself and took the form of a servant.

questions.topic: Christians living among non-Christians (1 Pet. 2:3-25; Rom. 15:1-2)
questions.stem: Peter teaches that servants should be submissive to their masters with all respect, not only to the kind and gentle but also to the
questions.explanation: 1 Pet. 2:18: "not only to the kind and gentle but also to the overbearing."

questions.stem: In Romans, Christians are admonished to put on the Lord Jesus Christ and not to
questions.explanation: Rom. 13:14: "put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make no provision for the flesh, to gratify its desires."

questions.stem: Paul teaches that those who have been baptized into Christ have been baptized into His
questions.explanation: Rom. 6:3: "all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death."

questions.stem: After their capture of the Ark of God, the Philistines discovered on the following days that
options: Dagon, their god, had fallen and broken to pieces
Dagon had disappeared from its place
the Ark had swallowed Dagon, their god
the Ark had been standing on Dagon
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 5:3-4: Dagon had fallen on his face before the ark, and the next morning his head and hands lay cut off on the threshold.

questions.stem: One of the sins of Manasseh for which the LORD sent bands of the Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites and Ammonites to destroy Judah was
options: the release of a thousand captives
his failure to obey God's prophets
the arrest of the King of Babylon
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 24:2-4: "for the sins of Manasseh... and also for the innocent blood that he had shed".

questions.stem: Elijah decreed that there would be neither rain nor dew for some years because
options: Ahab had forsaken the commandment of God by erecting an altar for Baal
Nebat the son of Rehoboam connived with Ahab to kill him
he was sure that he would be fed by the ravens
Jezebel the wife of Ahab killed Obadiah
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 16:31-17:1: Ahab served Baal and erected an altar for him; Elijah then announced the drought.

questions.stem: God called Jonah and sent him to the people of Nineveh to
options: pray to Him for their forgiveness
questions.explanation: Jonah 1:2: "Arise, go to Nineveh... and cry against it; for their wickedness has come up before me."

questions.stem: Consequent upon the murder of Naboth by Ahab and Jezebel, God declared that
options: dogs would lick Ahab's blood where they had licked Naboth's
Ahab's descendants would never ascend the throne in Israel
He would require the blood of Naboth from Ahab's hand
the sword would not depart from the house of Ahab
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 21:19: "In the place where dogs licked up the blood of Naboth shall dogs lick your own blood."

questions.topic: Social justice and true religion (Amos 2:6-8; 4; 5:1-25; 6:1-14; 7:10-17; 8:4-14; cf. James 1:19-27)
questions.stem: According to Amos, God decided to raise up a nation that would fight and oppress Israel because the people
options: were corrupt and enslaved the poor
claimed to achieve fame by their own strength
rejected him and sold the righteous for silver
questions.explanation: Amos 6:13-14: "you who say, Have we not by our own strength taken Karnaim for ourselves? For behold, I will raise up against you a nation".

questions.stem: What did King Josiah do to the altar that was erected by Jeroboam at Bethel?
options: He broke its stones into pieces
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 23:15: the altar at Bethel "he pulled down and he broke in pieces its stones, crushing them to dust".

questions.stem: According to Jeremiah, other nations would find glory in God and bless themselves in Him only when Israel
options: swears in truth, in justice and in uprightness
becomes loyal to God and repents of her sins
returns to God, honours and glorifies Him
comes to God with prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: Jer. 4:2: "if you swear, As the LORD lives, in truth, in justice, and in uprightness, then nations shall bless themselves in him, and in him shall they glory."

questions.stem: Hosea proclaimed that Israel should return to God and plead that he should
questions.explanation: Hos. 14:1-2: "Return, O Israel, to the LORD... say to him, Take away all iniquity."

questions.stem: The response of Eli after Samuel had told him the LORD's message as regards his sons' acts of blasphemy was that
options: sacrifice would be offered on their behalf
he would call them and rebuke them
God should have mercy on them
He was the LORD, and should do what pleased Him
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 3:18: "It is the LORD; let him do what seems good to him."

questions.stem: Rahab's reward for hiding the messengers sent by Joshua to spy out the city of Jericho was that
options: she and her household were spared
the city of Jericho was spared for her sake
she married one of the spies and became a queen
the gold, bronze and iron in the city were given to her
questions.explanation: Josh. 6:25: "Rahab the harlot, and her father's household, and all who belonged to her, Joshua saved alive."

questions.topic: Obedience and Rewards: Abraham (Gen. 22:1-19), the three Hebrew youths (Dan. 3:1-30), David (1 Sam. 30:1-20)
questions.stem: David's victory over the Amalekites who raided Ziklag was due to
options: the fact that David was a mighty man in battle
his swearing to the Egyptian servant of the Amalekites not to kill or harm him
the great army that followed him to fight the Amalekites
his prayer in seeking the approval of God before pursuing them
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 30:7-8: David inquired of the LORD, "Shall I pursue?" and was told, "Pursue; for you shall surely overtake".

questions.stem: God did not lead the Israelites by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near, because
options: He did not want them to see war and return to Egypt
the Egyptians would have overtaken them
they were afraid of the Philistines
He wanted them to learn through hardship in the wilderness
questions.explanation: Ex. 13:17: "Lest the people repent when they see war, and return to Egypt."

questions.topic: Unwise policies of Solomon and Rehoboam (1 Kings 9:15-23; 11:1-40; 12:1-20)
questions.stem: One of King Solomon's unwise policies was the
options: incessant fighting of wars against his enemies
signing of treaties with the kings of the surrounding nations
use of forced labour to build the house of God
making of sacrifices in high places
questions.explanation: 1 Kings 9:15: "the forced labour which King Solomon levied to build the house of the LORD" - a burden that led to the revolt under Rehoboam.

questions.stem: "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a helper fit for him." After this statement, the first thing God did was to
options: form beasts and birds and bring them to the man
take one of the man's ribs and close up its place with flesh
make a rib into a woman and bring her to the man
cause a deep sleep to fall upon the man
questions.explanation: Gen. 2:18-19: next, out of the ground the LORD formed every beast and bird and brought them to the man to name.

questions.stem: Joseph's brothers decided not to kill him because he
options: was their brother and their flesh
was the first son of his mother
questions.explanation: Gen. 37:27: "let not our hand be upon him, for he is our brother, our own flesh."

questions.stem: King Saul ordered that those who had opposed his ascent to the throne should not be put to death because
options: God had wrought deliverance in Israel
they had fought bravely in battle
they had been reconciled with him
God had forgiven their evil intentions
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 11:13: "No man shall be put to death this day, for today the LORD has wrought deliverance in Israel."

questions.stem: After Saul realized that God would have nothing to do with him, he sought the help of
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 28:6-7: when the LORD did not answer him, Saul said, "Seek out for me a woman who is a medium."

questions.stem: A promise made by King Saul to anyone that could face and defeat Goliath was
options: giving his daughter in marriage to the person
making the person second in command in Israel
giving the person part of his land
making the person the captain of his army
questions.explanation: 1 Sam. 17:25: the king "will give him his daughter, and make his father's house free in Israel".

questions.stem: The LORD said to Moses that the people should gather just a day's portion of bread so that He might test their
questions.explanation: Ex. 16:4: "that I may prove them, whether they will walk in my law or not."

questions.topic: God’s covenant with Israel (Ex. 19; 20; 24:1-11; cf. Deut. 28:1-19)
questions.stem: What were the Israelites asked to do before meeting with God on Mount Sinai?
options: To be consecrated and have their garments washed
To touch the border of the mountain
To fast and have their feet washed
To fast, pray and be consecrated
questions.explanation: Ex. 19:10: "consecrate them today and tomorrow, and let them wash their garments."

questions.topic: The Baptism and Temptation of Jesus
questions.stem: "To you I will give all this authority and their glory; for it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whom I will..." This statement was made during the
questions.explanation: Luke 4:5-6: the devil said this to Jesus during the temptation.

questions.topic: Parables about love of God (Mt. 18:12-14; Lk. 15:1-32)
questions.stem: "...Just so, I tell you, there is joy before the angels of God over one sinner who repents." Jesus made this statement after telling the parable of the
questions.explanation: Luke 15:8-10: the conclusion of the parable of the lost coin (the lost sheep ends with "joy in heaven").

questions.stem: According to Luke, the leper healed by Jesus was commanded to
options: go and show himself to his friends
find out from the priest what he should offer
make an offering for his cleansing
questions.explanation: Luke 5:14: "go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded."

questions.stem: After the great confession by Peter, Jesus charged the disciples to
options: announce that the kingdom of heaven had come
tell no one that he was the Christ
go away from the crowd to rest
beware of the leaven of the Pharisees
questions.explanation: Mt. 16:20: "he strictly charged the disciples to tell no one that he was the Christ."

questions.stem: The angel of the Lord told Zechariah that his son would
options: make the disobedient repent of their sins
turn many of the sons and daughters of Israel to God
go before God in the spirit and power of Elijah
turn the hearts of the children to their fathers
questions.explanation: Luke 1:17: "he will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah" (it is the hearts of the fathers that turn to the children).

questions.stem: When they returned from their mission, the seventy reported that
options: they saw Satan fall like lightning
even demons were subject to them
questions.explanation: Luke 10:17: "Lord, even the demons are subject to us in your name!"

questions.stem: "Take heart, it is I; have no fear." This statement was made by Jesus when
options: He appeared to two disciples on the way to Emmaus
He was walking on the sea in the night
Mary Magdalene saw him at the sepulchre
the women saw Him after the resurrection
questions.explanation: Mt. 14:25-27 / Mark 6:50: said as he came to them walking on the sea in the fourth watch of the night.

questions.topic: The Triumphal Entry and the Cleansing of the Temple
questions.stem: "...Blessed is the kingdom of our father David that is coming..." The declaration above was made by the crowd during the
questions.explanation: Mark 11:10: the crowds cried this as Jesus rode into Jerusalem.

questions.stem: After healing the man at the pool of Bethzatha, the Jews sought all the more to kill Jesus because
options: they hated the man that was healed
He did this on the Sabbath
they were unhappy that He healed the man
He claimed that God His Father was still working
questions.explanation: John 5:17-18: after Jesus said "My Father is working still, and I am working", they sought all the more to kill him because he called God his own Father, making himself equal with God.
